member.summary: Reads a CIM object. This function should be used to read CIM objects held as properties of other CIM objects.

member.summary: Gets the CIM type associated with a given CLSID.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.GetArrayOfCLSIDForExternalCIMType(System.Type)
member.summary: Gets the 'ArrayOf' CLSID for any external CIM types stored in arrays.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.StringSizeType
member.summary: The way the string size is written in streams (preceding the characters).

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.ReadString(System.IO.BinaryReader,ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.StringSizeType)
member.summary: Reads a string as written by native code.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.WriteString(System.String,System.IO.BinaryWriter,ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.BinaryUtil.StringSizeType)

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.CIM.CIM3DMarkerGraphic
member.summary: Represents a 3D marker graphic.

remarks.para: A 3DMarkerGraphic contains some properties that describe how the graphic is drawn (such as DiffuseColor, an optional URL to a texture image, and some material properties) and a URL pointing to a ShapeVertices structure that describes the marker's "geometry" (such as the vertex position, normal vector, and texture coordinates).

Because multiple 3DMarkerGraphics can reference the same ShapeVertices structure, an OffsetIntoShapeVertices and CountOfShapeVertices are provided to reference what records within the ShapeVertices correspond to this 3DMarkerGraphic.

The 3DMarkerGraphic also has an esri3DPrimitiveType that describes how those vertices are used to form shapes. These are analogous to the common primitive types in OpenGL, such as triangle strips and fans. Knowing what type of primitives are contained in this shape lets the reader determine how many Vertices are needed to form each primitive in the shape graphic.

member.summary: Represents a 3D marker which consists of one or more ShapeGraphics contained within one or more ShapeLODs.
member.remarks: A 3DShape Marker is a way to describe a 3D model with different levels of detail at different zoom levels. The ShapeLODs represent the same model at different levels of detail. member.summary:
This class is not for public use and is used internally by the system to implement support for other esri modules.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Data.InternalQueryFilter.DisjunctiveNormalFormTransformRecursive(ArcGIS.Core.Data.FullTextExpression)
member.summary: Get a new filter tree in disjunctive normal form.
member.param: The filter expression.
member.remarks:
Disjunctive normal form (DNF) is represented as OR statements of AND statements. This to facilitate how SQL processes these conditional operators, i.e. AND being higher precendence than OR.
For example, you have the 3 FullTextExpression objects (Q1, Q2, and Q3) and you want to represent this expression: Q1 AND (Q2 OR Q3). If this was simply processed from left to right, you would get the wrong expression because AND has precendence. You would get (Q1 AND Q2) OR Q3. Per DNF, you would expand the expression into an OR statement of 2 AND statements: (Q1 AND Q2) OR (Q1 AND Q3).
member.returns: The filter expression in disjunctive normal form.

member.summary: Perform a depth first search on the full text expression tree to get the filter information for ArcObjects.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Data.Knowledge.Analytics.AllPaths
member.summary: Represents all paths found by the Filtered Find Paths algorithm.
member.remarks:
This object uses a compact representation: if several paths use the same relationships groups, we have a single copy of the relationship group in this object.
On rare occasions, some path may be invalid, in this case returns null. A path is invalid if some entity or relationship that the path is using has been deleted in the graph while the pathfinding algorithm was running.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.CubicBezierBuilder
member.summary: Constructs a third degree CubicBezierSegment for use in a Multipart geometry.
member.remarks:
Use the CubicBezierBuilder class to to create and/or modify a CubicBezierSegment shape. A CubicBezierSegment is based upon the parent Segment class. The Segment class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the CubicBezierBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with a CubicBezierSegment. Use the CubicBezierBuilder.ToSegment method to get the CubicBezierSegment from the builder.
A cubic Bezier curve is a non-linear segment defined by four control points. The Bezier curve starts at control point 0 (start point) and ends at control point 3 (end point). The start point and control point 1 define the tangent at the start point. Control point 2 and the end point define the tangent at the end point. The length of these tangent lines and position of the 4 control points determines the shape of the created Bezier curve.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.EllipticArcBuilder
member.summary: Constructs an EllipticArcSegment for use in a Multipart geometry.
member.remarks:
Use the EllipticArcBuilder class to create and/or modify an EllipticArcSegment shape. An EllipticArcSegment is based upon the parent Segment class. The Segment class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the EllipticArcBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with an EllipticArcSegment. Use the EllipticArcBuilder.ToSegment method to get the EllipticArcSegment from the builder.
An elliptic arc is the portion of the boundary of a 2D ellipse that connects two points.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.EnvelopeBuilder
member.summary: Builder for creating an envelope.
member.remarks:
An envelope is an axis-aligned box described by the coordinates of the lower left corner and the coordinates of the upper right corner.
Use the EnvelopeBuilder class to to create and/or modify an Envelope shape. An Envelope is based upon the parent Geometry class. The Geometry class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the EnvelopeBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with an Envelope. Use the EnvelopeBuilder.ToGeometry method to get the Envelope geometry from the builder.

member.remarks:
If asRatio = false, the expansion is additive. If you want to increase the envelope width by 5 units, then dx = 5. On the other hand, if you want to decrease the envelope width by 5 units, then dx = -5. Similarly, set dy to increase or decrease the envelope height.
If asRatio = true, the expansion is multiplicative. If you want to increase the envelope width by 10%, then dx = 1.1. On the other hand, if you want to decrease the width by 10%, then dx = 0.9. Similarly, set dy to increase or decrease the envelope height. No negative numbers are allowed when asRatio is set to true.
The Envelope remains centered at the same position.
member.param: Change in x
Change in y
If asRatio = true, the expansion is multiplicative. If false, the expansion is additive.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.GeometryBagBuilder
member.summary: Builder for creating a GeometryBag.

remarks.para: Use the GeometryBagBuilder class to to create a GeometryBag shape. A GeometryBag is based upon the parent Geometry class. Use the GeometryBagBuilder.ToGeometry method to get the GeometryBag geometry from the builder.

The spatial reference of the GeometryBagBuilder is transferred (geometry projected if necessary) to any geometries added to it. However, the spatial reference of the added geometry is not transferred to the GeometryBagBuilder. Always make sure to set the spatial reference on the GeometryBagBuilder prior to adding other geometries to it to avoid creating invalid geometry. For example, adding geometries to a GeometryBagBuilder that doesn't have a well-defined spatial reference will set an unknown spatial reference to all the geometries added to the builder. Using the GeometryBag created from such a builder may cause unexpected behavior.
An Envelope is converted to a Polygon when it is inserted into a GeometryBag. As a result, when retrieving an Envelope from a GeometryBag, it will be a Polygon.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.LineBuilder
member.summary: Builder for creating a LineSegment.
member.remarks:
Use the LineBuilder class to to create and/or modify a LineSegment shape. A LineSegment is based upon the parent Segment class. The Segment class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the LineBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with a LineSegment. Use the LineBuilder.ToSegment method to get the LineSegment from the builder.
A line segment is a straight line between a start point and an end point.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.MultipartBuilder`1
member.summary: Abstract base class for the PolylineBuilder and PolygonBuilder classes.

remarks.para: Use the MultipartBuilder class to to create and/or modify a base Multipart shape. The builder is best suited for editing workflows where the user may be adding, inserting or removing parts of a Multipart geometry interactively. A Multipart is based upon the parent Geometry class. The Geometry class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the MultipartBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with a Multipart. Use the PolylineBuilder.ToGeometry or PolygonBuilder.ToGeometry method to get the Multipart from the builder.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.PolygonBuilder
member.summary: Builder for creating a polygon.

remarks.para: Use the PolygonBuilder class to to create and/or modify a Polygon shape. The builder is best suited for editing workflows where the user may be adding, inserting or removing parts of a Polygon geometry interactively. A Polygon are based upon the parent Geometry class. The Geometry class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the PolygonBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with a Polygon. Use the PolygonBuilder.ToGeometry method to get the Polygon geometry from the builder.

A polygon is defined by a collection of rings. Each ring is a collection of contiguous segments such that the start point and the end point of each are the same (that is it is a closed ring). If a polygon has more than one ring, the rings may be separate from one another or they may nest inside one another, but they should not overlap. Access the rings of a polygon using the method.

Note: For a polygon to be topologically correct, exterior rings should be clockwise and interior rings should be counterclockwise. If there is ever a doubt about the topological correctness of a polygon, call the GeometryEngine.SimplifyAsFeature method to correct any issues.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.PolylineBuilder
member.summary: Builder for creating a polyline.

remarks.para: Use the PolylineBuilder class to to create and/or modify a Polyline shape. The builder is best suited for editing workflows where the user may be adding, inserting or removing parts of a Polyline geometry interactively. A Polyline is based upon the parent Geometry class. The Geometry class is immutable which means that you can not change its shape once it is created. Hence, the PolylineBuilder provides the way to make changes when working with a Polyline. Use the PolylineBuilder.ToGeometry method to get the Polyline geometry from the builder.

A polyline is an ordered collection of paths where each path is a collection of contiguous segments. A has a start and an end point. If a polyline has more than one path, the paths may be separate from one another. The paths of a polyline can be obtained using the method.

Initializes a new instance of the class that is a linear approximation to a clothoid. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
The start point of the polyline. The tangent direction of the spiral, north azimuth, at the first point of the spiral. The unit of the azimuth is radians. The radius at the start of the spiral. The radius must be greater than zero. Double.Infinity is a valid value for the radius. The radius at the end of the spiral. The radius must be greater than zero. Double.Infinity is a valid value for the radius. The orientation of the spiral. The method of creation. signifies that specifies the length of the entire spiral. signifies that specifies the angle, in radians, measuring the span of the arc from the start to the end of the clothoid path. Either the length of the clothoid or the central angle of the clothoid as specified by . The method of densification. If is , then curveDensity is the maximum segment length allowed in the clothoid. If is , then curveDensity is the maximum distance, in meters, that the clothoid can deviate from the actual curve. If is , then curveDensity is the maximum angle between tangent lines to the curve.\ (Optional) The spatial reference of the polyline. The default value is null.A clothoid, also known as an Euler spiral, is a curve such that its curvature is equal to a constant times its length. Curvature is a value that measures how curved or flat the curve is at a point. The larger the curvature, the more flat the curve is. The curvature is equal to the reciprocal of the radius. If the radius is infinity, then the curvature is zero. i.e. flat.
Shown below is a clothoid with = 0, = double.PositiveInfinity, = 1, = , = , and = 10.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Geometry.ShapeType.Polygon
member.summary: A polygon consists of one or more rings. A ring is a connected sequence of four or more points that form a closed, non-self-intersecting loop. A polygon may contain multiple outer rings. The order of vertices or orientation for a ring indicates which side of the ring is the interior of the polygon. The neighborhood to the right of an observer walking along the ring in vertex order is the neighborhood inside the polygon. Vertices of rings defining holes in polygons are in a counterclockwise direction. Vertices for a single, ringed polygon are, therefore, always in clockwise order. The rings of a polygon are referred to as its parts.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnDataHandle``1(System.IntPtr,System.Boolean)
member.summary: This generic function should be used to wrap a handle with wrapper objects from the ArcGIS.Core.Data namespace only.
member.typeparam: The wrapper object type from the ArcGIS.Core.Data namespace.
member.param: The handle to be wrapped.
true if the reference count is incremented on . By default, it is false.
member.returns: The wrapper object of type or compatible with type . For example, you can wrap a feature class handle using type Table since FeatureClass is derived from Table. However, wrapping a true table handle using FeatureClass will return null. Likewise, you can wrap a feature handle using type Row since Feature is derived from Row, but wrapping a true row handle using Feature will return null. If cannot be wrapped using , null is returned.
member.remarks: If is a "borrowed" handle from an existing CoreObjectBase instance (i.e., a COM handle that has already been wrapped), it is critical that the caller passes in true for regardless of whether the returned wrapped object is explicitly disposed. The reason is that if the wrapped object's Dispose() is not explicitly called, the Garbage Collector will perform this task. When the time comes for IUnknown::Release() to be called on the underlying COM object, if there is a reference count mismatch, a crash will ensue.

member.summary: Represents 3D layer properties which contain properties used for 3D draw.

member.summary: Creates a default CIM3DLayerProperties object.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.CastShadows
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether shadows are enabled. If true, this layer's features contribute to shadows.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.IsLayerLit
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this layer is lit.
member.remarks: This property determines whether an object in 3D is shaded based on the angle of its normal compared to the lighting properties of the scene (where the "sun" is) or is lit uniformly as if by only ambient light (light with no distinct directionality).

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.LayerFaceCulling
member.summary: Gets or sets the layer's face culling setting.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.MaxDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum distance at which objects in view are visible. Objects beyond this point don't get rendered.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.MaxPreloadDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum radius from the camera at which objects outside the view are loaded. Values are in Meters.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.MinDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum distance at which objects in view are visible. Objects closer than this don't get rendered.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.MinPreloadDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum radius from the camera at which objects at which objects outside the view are loaded. Values are in Meters.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.PreloadTextureCutoffHigh
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance (in visible range) at which high resolution textures change to low resolution textures for objects outside the view. Range is 0 to 1.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.PreloadTextureCutoffLow
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance (in visible range) at which low resolution textures change to solid colors for objects outside the view. Range is 0 to 1.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.TextureCutoffHigh
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance (in visible range) at which high resolution textures change to low resolution textures. Range is 0 to 1.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.TextureCutoffLow
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance (in visible range) at which low resolution textures change to solid colors. Range is 0 to 1.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.TextureDownscalingFactor
member.summary: Gets or sets the downscaling factor. All textures for this layer are downscaled by this additional factor on loading.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.UseCompressedTextures
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether uncompressed textures are compressed using DXT5 at load time.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIM3DLayerProperties.VerticalExaggeration
member.summary: Gets or sets the layer's vertical exaggeration.

member.summary: Gets or sets the layer's exaggeration mode.

member.summary: Gets or sets the layer's vertical unit.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMBABenchmarkComparisonsProperties.DataSource
member.summary: Gets or sets the data source used in calculation of variables and standard geographies. Structure of the value is TYPE;COUNTRY_INFO;LOCAL_DATA_INFO where TYPE can be ONLINE, LOCAL, or CUSTOM. COUNTRY_INFO is country_id{|hierarchy}. For example, US|census or US. LOCAL_DATA_INFO is ID of local dataset. For example, USA_ESRI_2019. For example, for local US 2019 dataset it will be: "LOCAL;;USA_ESRI_2019". If online US data source is used, it may be "ONLINE;US|census;". Can be value of baDataSource GP GPEnvironment variable. https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/tool-reference/environment-settings/ba-data-source.htm.

member.summary: Represents Business Analyst Color Coded Layer Properties.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMBAColorCodedLayerParameters.DataSource
member.summary: Gets or sets the data source used in calculation of distances. Structure of the value is TYPE;COUNTRY_INFO;LOCAL_DATA_INFO where TYPE can be ONLINE, LOCAL, or CUSTOM. COUNTRY_INFO is country_id{|hierarchy}. For example, US|census or US. LOCAL_DATA_INFO is ID of local dataset. For example, USA_ESRI_2019. For example, for local US 2019 dataset it will be: "LOCAL;;USA_ESRI_2019". If online US data source is used, it may be "ONLINE;US|census;". Can be value of baDataSource GP GPEnvironment variable. https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/tool-reference/environment-settings/ba-data-source.htm.

member.summary: Represents a Business Analyst Suitability Analysis demographic variable-based criterion.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMBAVariableBasedCriterion.DataSource
member.summary: Gets or sets the data source used in calculation of distances. Structure of the value is TYPE;COUNTRY_INFO;LOCAL_DATA_INFO where TYPE can be ONLINE, LOCAL, or CUSTOM. COUNTRY_INFO is country_id{|hierarchy}. For example, US|census or US. LOCAL_DATA_INFO is ID of local dataset. For example, USA_ESRI_2019. For example, for local US 2019 dataset it will be: "LOCAL;;USA_ESRI_2019". If online US data source is used, it may be "ONLINE;US|census;". Can be value of baDataSource GP GPEnvironment variable. https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/tool-reference/environment-settings/ba-data-source.htm.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHuffModelDistanceParameters.DataSource
member.summary: Gets or sets data source used in calculation of distances. Structure of the value is TYPE;COUNTRY_INFO;LOCAL_DATA_INFO where TYPE can be ONLINE, LOCAL, or CUSTOM. COUNTRY_INFO is country_id{|hierarchy}. For example, US|census or US. LOCAL_DATA_INFO is ID of local dataset. For example, USA_ESRI_2019. For example, for local US 2019 dataset it will be: "LOCAL;;USA_ESRI_2019". If online US data source is used, it may be "ONLINE;US|census;". Can be value of baDataSource GP GPEnvironment variable. https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/tool-reference/environment-settings/ba-data-source.htm.

member.summary: A fixed list of colors for bivariate rendering. The count of colors should be equal to the number of breaks for each axis multiplied.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition
member.summary: Specifies the method of transition for a value in a keyframe.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.None
member.summary: The keyframe value is ignored.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.Linear
member.summary: Value changes at a constant (linear) rate to the end state.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.Stepped
member.summary: Value switches to the end state at a specified point along the transition.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.Hop
member.summary: Value increases, using a parabolic curve, beyond the end state before returning back to it. The height of the curve can be configured.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.FixedArc
member.summary: Value changes along a tightly controlled curve to the end state.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.AdjustableArc
member.summary: Value changes along a smooth curve to the end state. The tightness of the curve can be configured.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.AnimationTransition.Hold
member.summary: Value remains constant, equaling the previous keyframe's value.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsConfiguration.ClosedPathPolicy
member.summary:
Gets or sets the closed path policy, i.e whether we allow, forbid, or require that the start and end vertices of a path are equal.
When the value is KGClosedPathPolicy.Require, the DestinationEntities field is ignored and destinations entities are the same as origin entities.

member.summary: Gets or sets the origin entities.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsConfiguration.DestinationEntities
member.summary:
Gets or sets the destination entities.
This field is ignored when ClosedPathPolicy is KGClosedPathPolicy.Require.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage
member.summary: Specifies how origin/destination entities are used in the filtered find paths algorithm.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage.AnyOriginAnyDestination
member.summary: The filtered find paths algorithm only returns the shortest paths for the origin entities that have the shortest shortest paths and the shortest paths for the destination entities that have the shortest shortest paths. When multiple entities are used, this option leads to faster computations.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage.AnyOriginAllDestinations
member.summary: The filtered find paths algorithm returns the shortest paths for the origin entities that have the shortest shortest paths and one shortest path (if it exists) per destination entity. When multiple entities are used, this option leads to longer computations.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage.AllOriginsAnyDestination
member.summary: The filtered find paths algorithm returns one shortest path (if it exists) per origin entity and the shortest paths for the destination entities that have the shortest shortest paths. When multiple entities are used, this option leads to longer computations.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage.AllOriginsAllDestinations
member.summary: The filtered find paths algorithm returns one shortest path (if it exists) per origin entity and one shortest path (if it exists) per destination entity. When multiple entities are used, this option leads to longer computations.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.FilteredFindPathsEntityUsage.EachPair
member.summary: The filtered find paths algorithm returns one shortest path (if it exists) per pair of origin and destination entity. When multiple entities are used, this option leads to longer computations. An error will be returned if strictly more than 10 origin entities are defined or if strictly more than 10 destination entities are defined.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics
member.summary:
Represents the statistics related to a Filtered Find Paths search.
It contains the size of the local graph, and the number of openCypher "expansion" queries that have been issued to construct the local graph.
The local graph is an in-memory graph used for pathfinding where a node represents an entity in the Knowledge Graph and an edge represents one or many parallel relationships in the Knowledge Graph.
The local graph typically contains (much) less nodes than the Knowledge Graph, but enough nodes and edges to ensure that the pathfinding results are accurate. For example, to guarantee that all paths of length up to 'L' between 'A' and 'B' are present in the local graph, we ensure that the sum of counts of "expansion" queries related to 'A' and 'B' is greater or equal to 'L'.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics.CountLocalGraphNodes
member.summary: Gets or sets the count of nodes in the local graph.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics.CountLocalGraphEdges
member.summary: Gets or sets the count of edges in the local graph.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics.CountOriginExpansionQueries
member.summary: Gets or sets the count of expansion queries that were done to discover the neighborhood of some origin entities.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics.CountDestinationExpansionQueries
member.summary: Gets or sets the count of expansion queries that were done to discover the neighborhood of some destination entities.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFilteredFindPathsStatistics.CountWaypointsExpansionQueries
member.summary: Gets or sets the count of expansion queries that were done to discover the neighborhood of entity or relationship waypoints.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions
member.summary:
Rules defining which "successor" events are allowed to be after a given "predecessor" event.
One implied rule is that a successor event must start at or after the start of the predecessor event.
These rules use the notions of "Gap" and "Overlap" defined hereunder.
Definition of "Overlap": When the successor event start is before the predecessor event end, the overlap is the time from the successor event start to the predecessor event end. When the successor event start is after the predecessor event end, the overlap is zero.
Definition of "Gap": When the successor event start is before the predecessor event end, the gap is zero. When the successor event start is after the predecessor event end, the gap is the time from the predecessor event end to the successor event start.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.RestrictMaxOverlap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the max overlap is restricted.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.MaxOverlap
member.summary:
Gets or sets the max overlap between consecutive events. The unit of this value is MaxOverlapUnit.
This value is taken into account only if RestrictMaxOverlap is true.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.MaxOverlapUnit
member.summary:
Gets or sets the unit of MaxOverlap.
Accepted values are { esriTimeUnitsMilliseconds, esriTimeUnitsSeconds, esriTimeUnitsMinutes, esriTimeUnitsHours, esriTimeUnitsDays, esriTimeUnitsWeeks }.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.RestrictMaxGap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the max gap is restricted.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.MaxGap
member.summary:
Gets or sets the max gap. The unit of this value is MaxGapUnit.
This value is taken into account only if RestrictMaxGap is true.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGConsecutiveEventsRestrictions.MaxGapUnit
member.summary:
Gets or sets the unit of MaxGap.
Accepted values are { esriTimeUnitsMilliseconds, esriTimeUnitsSeconds, esriTimeUnitsMinutes, esriTimeUnitsHours, esriTimeUnitsDays, esriTimeUnitsWeeks }.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGPaths
member.summary:
Represents the paths found by the Filtered Find Paths search.
We use a memory-optimized representation to avoid storing redundant information because it is often the case that a path shares some entities and relationships with many other paths, especially if the Filtered Find Paths configuration uses 'KGPathMode.All'.
Definition: a relationship group contains Knowledge Graph relationships associated to a single edge in the local graph.
Paths are encoded this way:
The path 'p' uses relationships groups PathsBuffer[PathsEndIndex[p-1] .. PathsEndIndex[p]], and: - the origin of the first relationship group is the origin of the path - the destination of the last relationship group is the destination of the path
A path of length zero (with entity 'e') has a single relationship group containing no relationship and where the origin and the destination are 'e'.
The relationships group 'g' has origin EntitiesUIDs[RelationshipsGroupsFrom[g]], destination EntitiesUIDs[RelationshipsGroupsTo[g]]. Its relationships are RelationshipsGroupsUIDsBuffer[RelationshipsGroupsUIDsEndIndex[g-1] .. RelationshipsGroupsUIDsEndIndex[g]].
The relationship RelationshipsGroupsUIDsBuffer[i] has a cost RelationshipsCosts[i].
if RelationshipsFrom[i] >= 0, relationship RelationshipsGroupsUIDsBuffer[i] has origin EntitiesUIDs[RelationshipsFrom[i]] else the relationship has been deleted after pathfinding.
if RelationshipsTo[i] >= 0, relationship RelationshipsGroupsUIDsBuffer[i] has destination EntitiesUIDs[RelationshipsTo[i]] else the relationship has been deleted after pathfinding.
Note that origin and destination of a relationship may not match origin and destination of the relationship group because the relationship can be traversed backwards.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGPaths.EntitiesUIDs
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of entities that may be used in paths (not all entities are guaranteed to be used).

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGPaths.EntityTypes
member.summary:
Gets or sets a list parallel to EntitiesUIDs representing entity type indices.
if EntityTypes[i] >= 0, EntitiesUIDs[i] has type IndexedEntityTypes[EntityTypes[i]] else the entity has been deleted after the find path operation.

if RelationshipTypes[i] >= 0, RelationshipsGroupsUIDsBuffer[i] has type IndexedRelationshipTypes[RelationshipTypes[i]] else the relationship has been deleted after the find path operation.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGTimeFilter
member.summary: A Knowledge Graph Time Filter represents a set of time constraints that apply to the "events" of a path.
member.remarks:
"Events" are entities and relationships of the path that have a matching in .
A CIMKGEventDefinition can either be durative (one property represents the start time, and one property representing the end time) or "punctual" (a single property represents the time at which the event occurs).
The time filter represents three kinds of time constraints:
- constraints that are applied to all events of the path (),
- constraints that are applied only to durative events of the path ().
- constraints that are applied to all pairs of consecutive events of the path ( and ).
The time filter also specifies the behavior when an event has missing or ill-formed time information ().

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGTimeFilter.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the filter is enabled.
member.remarks: Having an empty list of event definitions in is equivalent to not enabling the time filter.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGTimeFilter.KGPathTimeFlow
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating how time should flow along the result paths.
member.remarks:
The define rules that apply to each pair (A, B) of consecutive events, enforcing that event B is a valid "successor" of event A (event A is then called a valid "predecessor" of event B).
- When time flows forward, for each pair of consecutive events, the event which is closer to the path origin must be a valid predecessor of the event which is closer to the path destination.
- When time flows backward, for each pair of consecutive events, the event which is closer to the path origin must be a valid successor of the event which is closer to the path destination.
- When the time flow is not constrained, for each pair of consecutive events, the event which is closer to the path origin must either be a valid successor or a valid predecessor of the event which is closer to the path destination.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGTimeFilter.TimeWindow
member.summary: Gets or sets the time window. Any event that has a time span not intersecting the time window will be excluded.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKGTimeFilter.EventsDefinitions
member.summary: Gets or sets the events definitions.
member.remarks: If no event is defined, it is as if the time filter was disabled. The time filter will have no effect on path finding.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration
member.summary:
Represents the Centrality computation options for a Knowledge Graph.
Several measures of centrality are supported: Degree, Indegree, Outdegree, PageRank, Eigenvector, Coreness, Betweenness, Closeness and Harmonic.
These measures fall in two broad categories: degree based measures are Degree, Indegree, Outdegree, PageRank, Eigenvector and Coreness while shortest paths based measures are Betweenness, Closeness and Harmonic.
The "importance" relationship weight is taken into account in degree based measures: a relationship with higher importance will increase the centrality scores of nearby related entities.
The "cost" relationship weight is taken into account in shortest paths based measures: a relationship with higher cost will decrease the centrality scores of nearby related entities.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipsInterpretation
member.summary: Gets or sets the relationships interpretation.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.DefaultRelationshipImportance
member.summary: Gets or sets the default importance of a relationship.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipImportanceProperty
member.summary:
Gets or sets the property defining the importance of a relationship.
When the string is empty, or the property doesn't exist, or the property value is null, the default relationship importance is used instead.
Negative property values are ignored and replaced by zero.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.DefaultRelationshipCost
member.summary: Gets or sets the default cost of a relationship.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipCostProperty
member.summary:
Gets or sets the property defining the cost of a relationship.
When the string is empty, or the property doesn't exist, or the property value is null, the default relationship cost is used instead.
Negative property values are ignored and replaced by zero.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.MultiedgeFactor
member.summary:
Gets or sets the multiedge factor. Acceptable values lie in [0, 1].
In centrality computations, we reduce parallel relationships of a graph to a single edge.
The computation of the importance of the single edge depends on the value of MultiedgeFactor.
If MultiedgeFactor is 0, the importance of the single edge is the average of parallel relationships. If MultiedgeFactor is 1, the importance of the single edge is the sum of importances of parallel relationships. For values of MultiedgeFactor between 0 and 1, the importance of the single edge is linearly interpolated.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.Normalization
member.summary: Gets or sets the scores normalization.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the coordinate should be interpreted as long,lat (true) or lat,lon(false,default). This value only has meaning when the coordinate is ambiguous. For example, the coordinate "34N 22E" is not ambiguous as the latitude and longitude are both defined by the coordinate. However, "34 22" is ambiguous since it could mean either "34N 22E" or "34E 22N". In this situation the value of this property determines the recognized coordinate.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration
member.summary:
Represents the Centrality computation options in a Knowledge Graph Link Chart.
Several measures of centrality are supported: Degree, Indegree, Outdegree, PageRank, Eigenvector, Coreness, Betweenness, Closeness and Harmonic.
These measures fall in two broad categories: degree based measures are Degree, Indegree, Outdegree, PageRank, Eigenvector and Coreness while shortest paths based measures are Betweenness, Closeness and Harmonic.
The "importance" relationship weight is taken into account in degree based measures: a relationship with higher importance will increase the centrality scores of nearby related entities.
The "cost" relationship weight is taken into account in shortest paths based measures: a relationship with higher cost will decrease the centrality scores of nearby related entities.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipsInterpretation
member.summary: Gets or sets the relationships interpretation.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.ComputeShortestPathsBasedMeasures
member.summary:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the shortest paths based measures will be computed.
When true, all measures are computed. When false, all measures except betweenness, Closeness, Harmonic are computed.
This setting exists because shortest paths based measures can be costly to compute for larger graphs.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.IncludeDocumentEntities
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether entities of type 'Document' are considered to be part of the graph for centrality computations.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.DefaultRelationshipImportance
member.summary: Gets or sets the default importance of a relationship.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipImportanceProperty
member.summary:
Gets or sets the property defining the importance of a relationship.
When the string is empty, or the property doesn't exist, or the property value is null, the default relationship importance is used instead.
Negative property values are ignored and replaced by zero.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.DefaultRelationshipCost
member.summary: Gets or sets the default cost of a relationship.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.RelationshipCostProperty
member.summary:
Gets or sets the property defining the cost of a relationship.
When the string is empty, or the property doesn't exist, or the property value is null, the default relationship cost is used instead.
Negative property values are ignored and replaced by zero.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.MultiedgeFactor
member.summary:
Gets or sets the multiedge factor. Acceptable values lie in [0, 1].
In centrality computations, we reduce parallel relationships of a graph to a single edge.
The computation of the importance of the single edge depends on the value of MultiedgeFactor.
If MultiedgeFactor is 0, the importance of the single edge is the average of parallel relationships. If MultiedgeFactor is 1, the importance of the single edge is the sum of importances of parallel relationships. For values of MultiedgeFactor between 0 and 1, the importance of the single edge is linearly interpolated.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeGraphLinkChartCentralityConfiguration.Normalization
member.summary: Gets or sets the scores normalization.

member.summary: Gets or sets the time axis direction.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.TimeBannerUTCOffsetInMinutes
member.summary: Gets or sets the UTC offset of the time banner, in minutes.

member.summary: Gets or sets the event ticks visualization option. Event ticks are displayed in the time banner.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.ShowDurationLineForNonZeroDurationEntityEvents
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether lines representing the duration of events with non-zero durations are shown.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.DurationLineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the width of the line, in points, representing the duration of an event with non-zero duration.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.EntityPositionAtDurationRatio
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating where the entity of a non-zero duration event will be placed. 0.0 represents the start of the duration interval, 1.0 represents the end of the duration interval. Used in multi-timeline layout only.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.ShowNonZeroDurationIntervalBounds
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether duration interval bounds are represented in relationship lines of events that have non-zero durations. Used in multi-timeline layout only.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.SeparateTimeOverlaps
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether events that overlap in time are separated.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.SeparateTimelineOverlaps
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether events that overlap on a timeline are separated.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.MoveFirstBends
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the first bend on a relationship line related to an event is moved higher up from the event location when some events are separated. Used only in the mono-timeline layout, when 'SeparateTimelineOverlaps' is true.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.SecondBendRatio
member.summary: Gets or sets the ratio at which the second bend or a relationship occurs, for event relationships and non-event relationships between events and non-event entities. Used only in the mono-timeline layout.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.LineSeparationMultiplier
member.summary: Gets or sets the multiplier used for line separation. Lines will be more separated with a higher multiplier.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.SpaceSeparatedLinesEvenly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether separated lines are spaced evenly. When true, the offset for the i-th overlapping line is proportional to 'i'. When false, the offset for the i-th overlapping line is proportional to 'squareRoot(i)'.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.UseBezierCurves
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use Bezier curves to represent separated lines.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartChronologicalLayoutSettings.SeparatedLineShapeRatio
member.summary: Gets or sets the separated line shape ratio. When the ratio is high, the angle between the extremities of the separated line geometry and the original line is small.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartOrganicLayoutSettings
member.summary: Contains settings to be used in organic layout calculations.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartOrganicLayoutSettings.ComputationTimeBudget
member.summary: Gets or sets the computation time budget, in seconds. The maximum count of iterations of the force directed algorithm is computed based on the size of the link chart and this computation budget, assuming computations are executed by a theoretical CPU with some known characteristics. Higher values lead to better looking layouts.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartOrganicLayoutSettings.AbsoluteIdealEdgeLength
member.summary: Gets or sets the value, in degrees, to use for the ideal edge length during layout calculations when the IdealEdgeLengthType is 'absoluteValue'. Only used for geographic layouts.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartOrganicLayoutSettings.MultiplicativeIdealEdgeLength
member.summary: Gets or sets the value used to multiply the default edge length to determine the ideal edge length during layout calculations, when the IdealEdgeLengthType is 'multiplier'. Only used for geographic layouts.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMKnowledgeLinkChartOrganicLayoutSettings.IdealEdgeLengthType
member.summary: Gets or sets the ideal edge length type which determines which property to use to compute the ideal edge length. Only used for geographic layouts. When the value is 'AbsoluteValue', the 'AbsoluteIdealEdgeLength' property is used. When the value is 'Multiplier', the 'MultiplicativeIdealEdgeLength' property is used.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMLayout
member.summary: Represents a layout in a project.

remarks.para: A layout is a collection of visual elements arranged on a logical sheet of paper. A layout in a GIS is typically used to display one or more maps at a particular extent and scale. The layout is used to compose a presentation of data, describe the maps, and/or tell a story of the map data.

A layout defines a logical sheet of paper. It has a height and a width, and also a linear unit used to display positions on the page. It can have a snapping grid and a set of guides to help users arrange its elements.
The layout contains an ordered list of elements. When the layout draws, it tells each element to draw, in order.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMMap
member.summary: Represents a map or scene.

remarks.para: A map is a container of geographic information. There are different kinds of geographic information within a map: imagery, terrain, and different kinds of vector data. The information in a map is organized into layers. A map contains an ordered list of layers, and draws each layer on top of its preceding layers. In 3D layers may be drawn in Z order and not layer order.

A map has a single spatial reference system. Each of its layers can be stored natively in different spatial reference systems. If a layer has a different spatial reference system than a map it is displayed in, the map reprojects the data to its spatial reference system before drawing it.
A map can dynamically place labels for its features. It finds optimal label locations for each map extent to maximize typographic clarity and to avoid overlaps.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer
member.summary: Represents a heat map renderer. The heat map renderer draws point features as a continuous color gradient representing the density of the points. The resulting density surface represents the physical proximity between points, optionally weighted by a specified attribute value. The displayed raster surface is dynamic and updates if the source point features are edited.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.ColorScheme
member.summary: Gets or sets the color scheme of the heat map. Controls how smooth the color gradient appears. Must be either a continuous or multipart color ramp. If no color scheme is specified, a default color ramp will be used.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.Field
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the field denoting weighting values for each feature. The field's value is the count or quantity to be spread across the landscape to create a continuous surface. Values in the field may be integer or floating point. The options for the field are listed below. Specify the name of a numeric field in the feature table Use "" if no item or special value will be used and each feature will be counted once. Use Shape if input features contains Z.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.Radius
member.summary: Gets or sets the radius which defines how far the heat spreads away from the points. Specified and stored in Points and translates to Pixels at draw time.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.RendererQuality
member.summary: Gets or sets the renderer quality which controls the pixelation of the raster. This is an arbitrary range that goes from Best (10) to Fastest (0).

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.Heading
member.summary: Gets or sets the legend heading.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMHeatMapRenderer.MinLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets the legend label for the minimum density value.

member.summary: Gets or sets the legend label for the maximum density value.

member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum pixel intensity.

member.summary: Gets or sets the pixel intensity stops.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to update renderers pixel intensity range automatically. When set to True renderer's pixel intensity range will change based on the features with in the visible extent.

member.summary: Gets or sets the scale at which the search radius (in screen units - points) is converted to map units.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCallout
member.summary: Represents a callout.
member.remarks: Callouts are used to define additional ornamentation for a symbol. The primary use for callouts is to add leader line capabilities to text. Callouts are also used for defining items such as highway shields, balloon callouts, and more complex text box and leader line combinations. All callouts have some capability to draw leader lines; therefore they share a base property of a leader tolerance.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCallout.LeaderTolerance
member.summary: Gets or sets the leader tolerance which is the closest distance (in points) to the text the anchor point can be for the callout to draw.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCallout.LeaderOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the leader offset which is an offset value defining the distance (in points) between the anchor point and the beginning of the drawn leader.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCharacterMarker
member.summary: Represents a character marker.
member.remarks: The shape of a marker is defined by a glyph in a font. The marker is drawn using the specified size and color. Each marker has a defined frame around the glyph that is considered when the size is applied. As a result, character markers of the same size may appear different sizes if the glyphs frames are different sizes.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout
member.summary: Represents a composite callout. Composite callouts are a filled background along with an optional shadow, which is placed behind text. They may also have a leader line (consisting of one or both of a simple line, and filled dart) connecting the callout to an anchor point. Composite callouts may have additional surrounding text elements. The text representing these parts is specified in the text string using tags. Their relative position properties are specified in the CIMCompositeCallout through their corresponding CIMCompositeTextPartPosition elements specified below, but these properties can also be overridden with tag attributes.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.CornerRadius
member.summary: Gets or sets the callout corner radius in points. 0.0 corresponds to a rectangle corner.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.BackgroundSymbol
member.summary: Gets or sets the symbol used to draw the background.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.Margin
member.summary: Gets or sets the text margin defining the space around the text that is accounted for in balloon creation.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.DartWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the dart width.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.DartSymbol
member.summary: Gets or sets a symbol used to draw the dart. This is only used if LeaderLinePercentage is less than 100%.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.SnapLeaderToCornersOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the leader line should snap only to corners.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.LeaderLinePercentage
member.summary: Gets or sets the percentage of the leader line which is drawn as a line as opposed to a solid dart.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.LeaderLineSymbol
member.summary: Gets or sets the leader line symbol. This is only used if LeaderLinePercentage is greater than 0%.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.ShadowSymbol
member.summary: Gets or sets the shadow symbol for the callout.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.ShadowXOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the shadow offset from the callout symbol in the horizontal direction. If X and Y are zero, no shadow is drawn.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.ShadowYOffset
member.summary: Gets or sets the shadow offset from the callout symbol in the vertical direction. If X and Y are zero, no shadow is drawn.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.Middle
member.summary: Gets or sets the text part position properties for the middle part of the callout text. This contains the relative positioning information. Split offset and box will have no effect on this text part, since it is required that the middle part is in the center of the callout.

member.summary: Gets or sets the text part position properties for the top left part of the callout text. This contains the relative positioning information, as well as split offset indicating the extent to which the callout part will mask the callout outline, and whether or not the part should be boxed in by the overall callout, or not.

member.summary: Gets or sets the text part position properties for the bottom part of the callout text. This contains the relative positioning information, as well as split offset indicating the extent to which the callout part will mask the callout outline, and whether or not the part should be boxed in by the overall callout, or not.

member.summary: Gets or sets the text part position properties for the bottom right part of the callout text. member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeCallout.Floating
member.summary: Gets or sets the text part position properties for the floating part of the callout text. This contains the relative positioning information, as well as split offset indicating the extent to which the callout part will mask the callout outline, and whether or not the part should be boxed in by the overall callout, or not. The floating part is anchored below the bottom text part. If there is no bottom text part it is anchored below the middle text part plus margins.

member.summary: Gets or sets the split offset of the text part. This determines how much of a gap there is between the callout border and any part of the text part intersecting the border If this is set to wider than the callout width, none of the associated callout line will draw.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMCompositeTextPartPosition.IsPartWithinCalloutBox
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the text part will be contained within the main callout. If this is set to true, the main callout will expand to encompass this text part, and a line will be draw separating the part from the rest of the callout. This line will have the same symbol as the callout outline and will only draw if the text part is above or below the top and bottom margins of the middle text.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.FullGeometry
member.summary: Default: returns the input line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PerpendicularFromFirstSegment
member.summary: Third vertex to first segment midpoint.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ReversedFirstSegment
member.summary: Line between vertex 2 and vertex 1. Line begins at vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PerpendicularToSecondSegment
member.summary: Second segment midpoint to first vertex.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.SecondSegmentWithTicks
member.summary: Line between vertex 2 and vertex 3 with ticks on ends.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.DoublePerpendicular
member.summary: Two lines perpendicular to the first segment. Length of the lines is determined by vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.OppositeToFirstSegment
member.summary: Lines perpendicular to vertex 3 and the midpoint of the first segment with the length determined by first segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.TriplePerpendicular
member.summary: Three lines perpendicular to the first segment. Length of the lines is determined by vertex 3. Top and bottom lines stop at 80% of first segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.HalfCircleFirstSegment
member.summary: Half circle centered on the midpoint of first segment. Orientation is opposite vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.HalfCircleSecondSegment
member.summary: Half circle ending on vertex 2 opposite vertex 1. Diameter is defined by vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.HalfCircleExtended
member.summary: U shaped line with curve between vertex 2 and vertex 3. Control points on vertex 1 and vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.OpenCircle
member.summary: 330 degrees circle centered on vertex 1 starting at vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.CoverageEdgesWithTicks
member.summary: Lines between vertex 1 to vertex 3 and vertex 2 to vertex 4. Angled ticks at the end of the lines and vertex 1 and vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.GapExtentWithDoubleTicks
member.summary: Two lines with angled ticks on end. Lines created between first and third segments.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.GapExtentMidline
member.summary: Line centered between first and third segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.Chevron
member.summary: Chevron with apex at vertex 1 and ends at vertex 2 and vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PerpendicularWithArc
member.summary: Line between vertex 1 and vertex 2 with arc off of vertex 2. Cross line is perpendicular to vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ClosedHalfCircle
member.summary: Semi-circle with vertex 1 and vertex 2 at the corners.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.TripleParallelExtended
member.summary: Three parallel lines of varying length connected to a base line. The base defined by first segment. Vertex 3 is the end of the longest line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ParallelWithTicks
member.summary: Line with angled ticks on ends between vertex 1 and vertex 2 with a mirrored parallel line placed at the width defined by vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.Parallel
member.summary: Line between vertex 1 and vertex 2 with a parallel line placed at the width defined by vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PerpendicularToFirstSegment
member.summary: Line perpendicular to the midpoint of first segment. Length X% longer than vertex 2-vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ParallelOffset
member.summary: Parallels lines offset from first segment. Offset determined by vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.OffsetOpposite
member.summary: Single line offset from first segment. Offset to opposite side as vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.OffsetSame
member.summary: Single line offset from first segment. Offset to same side as vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.CircleWithArc
member.summary: Circle centered on vertex 1 with attached arc. Vertex 3 determines the side of the 90 degree arc. If 3 points, vertex 2 determines the length of the arc. If 4 points, vertex 2 determines the radius of the circle and vertex 4 determines the length of the arc.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.DoubleJog
member.summary: Two lines with jogs with gap in between. If there is 3 points the gap is centered on vertex. If 4 points the gap is defined by second segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PerpendicularOffset
member.summary: Line perpendicular from midpoint of second segment. End point is offset from second segment. Vertex 1 sets length of line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.LineExcludingLastSegment
member.summary: Line between vertex 1 and vertex N-1.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.MultivertexArrow
member.summary: Multipoint arrow. Vertex 1 sets the tip and vertex N the width and back of the arrowhead.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.CrossedArrow
member.summary: Multipoint arrow. Vertex 1 sets the tip and vertex N the width and back of the arrowhead. Crossed at midpoint between vertex 1 and vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ChevronArrow
member.summary: Chevron arrow centered on vertex 1.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ChevronArrowOffset
member.summary: Chevron arrow centered on vertex 1 offset towards vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.PartialFirstSegment
member.summary: Line along first segment, starting at vertex 2 extending in the direction and length of vertex 3.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.Arch
member.summary: 3 point arched line between vertex 1 and vertex 2. Vertex 3 determines the depth of the arch.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.CurvedParallelTicks
member.summary: Curved line with ticks. Curve begins on vertex 2 and ends on vertex 3. Ticks on opposite side of vertex 1.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.Arc90Degrees
member.summary: 90 degree arc with ends at vertex 1 and vertex 2. Vertex 3 determines the side of the curve.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.TipWithPerpendicularAndTicks
member.summary: Dynamic line perpendicular to segment 1, center on vertex 1 and offset towards vertex 2 with ticks.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ConcentricCircles
member.summary: Creates 2 or 3 concentric circles centered on vertex 1. Circle radius is based on vertex location.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.DoubleJogArrow
member.summary: Creates two dynamic lines with jogs centered on vertex 1.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.LinkedChevrons
member.summary: Creates a dynamic line between vertex 1 and 2 connecting two chevrons. Vertex 3 defines the width of the chevrons.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.SegmentThenHalfCircle
member.summary: Creates a dynamic line with a straight segment followed by a half circle. The diameter of the circle is determined by the length of the second segment. Vertex 4 determines the side of the half circle.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.LineWithStraightTicks
member.summary: Creates a dynamic line with vertex 1 in the middle. Vertices 2 and 3 define the length of the ticks and the line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.DoubleCurve
member.summary: Creates a dynamic line with alternating curves at vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.ParallelWithTicksByWidth
member.summary: Creates a dynamic line with angled ticks on the ends between vertex 2 and vertex 3. A mirrored parallel line is placed at the width defined by vertex 2.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.GeometricEffectControlMeasureLineRule.EnclosingRoundedRectangle
member.summary: Creates an enclosing rectangle around the line with rounded corners.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle
member.summary: The style of line to generate when a leader is drawn defined by an enumeration value. Line leaders will always be drawn with their own geometry.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.Base
member.summary: The line callout leader is a single line originating from the closest corner of the text box with the gap applied. If the callout has an accent bar it is connected to the closest point at the either top or bottom of the accent bar.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.MidPoint
member.summary: The line callout leader is a single line originating from the midpoint of the left or right side of the text box with the gap applied or from the midpoint of the accent bar if the callout has one.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.ThreePoint
member.summary: The line callout leader is a 3-point line originating from the midpoint of the left or right side of the text box with the gap applied or the midpoint of the accent bar if the callout has one.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.FourPoint
member.summary: The line callout leader is a 4-point line originating from the midpoint of the left or right side of the text box with the gap applied or the midpoint of the accent bar if the callout has one.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.Underline
member.summary: The line callout draws a line that connects to the closest of the four corners of the text with the gap applied. If the callout has an accent bar it is connected to the closest point at either the top or bottom of the accent bar. Additionally, either and underline or an "overline" is drawn along the closest side (bottom or top) of the text.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.CircularCW
member.summary: The line callout leader is curved (clockwise) from the anchor point to the closest corner of the text box with the gap applied. If the callout has an accent bar it is connected to the closest point at the either top or bottom of the accent bar.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LeaderLineStyle.CircularCCW
member.summary: The line callout leader is curved (counter-clockwise) from the anchor point to the closest corner of the text box with the gap applied. If the callout has an accent bar it is connected to the closest point at the either top or bottom of the accent bar.

member.summary: Determines how the strokes with dash patterns and other patterns (tiled pictures, placement effects) are handled at the end points of the line geometry's segments.
member.remarks: If more than one pattern exists (for example, a dashed simple stroke, a hash stroke, and a marker stroke) then the longest pattern's length is affected directly by this option and the rest of the stroke patterns are resized proportionately to match.

member.summary: No Constraint - no constraint is applied to how the dash is placed.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LineDashEnding.HalfPattern
member.summary: Half Pattern - a half dash will be placed on either side of control points.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LineDashEnding.HalfGap
member.summary: Half Gap - a space equal to the half the gap value will be placed on either side of control points.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LineDashEnding.FullPattern
member.summary: Full Pattern - a full dash will be placed on either side of control points.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LineDashEnding.FullGap
member.summary: Full Gap - a space equal to the gap value will be placed on either side of control points.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.LineDashEnding.Custom
member.summary: Custom - the pattern is fit to the length of the feature by adjusting the gaps slightly.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMShapeVertex
member.summary: Represents a shape vertex.
member.remarks: Each Vertex in a 3DShapeGraphic is represented by three points, contained in a ShapeVertex. The first point is the actual position of the Vertex. The second represents the normalized vector that describes the orientation of the point. The last point is optional - it defines the coordinates of the texture that correspond with this point in the shape. In this case only x and y are used as the traditional texture coordinates S and T.

member.summary: Defines the vertical anchor used to render the simple 3D line style in relation to the ground in 3D. This property is ignored for the Strip style which is drawn flat upon the surface, and for the Wall style which always uses a Bottom anchor.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.Simple3DLineAnchor.Center
member.summary: The center of the 3D line style is vertically aligned with the ground. The 3D line style is rendered both above and under the ground as a result.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.Simple3DLineAnchor.Bottom
member.summary: The 3D line style is rendered above the ground as the vertical anchor is set to the bottom of the style.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.Simple3DLineAnchor.Top
member.summary: The 3D line style is rendered under the ground as the vertical anchor is set to the top of the style.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to draw the text in a fashion compatible with ArcMap.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMTextSymbol.CountryISO
member.summary: Gets or sets the ISO code for the base country of the text.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMTextSymbol.Depth3D
member.summary: Gets or sets the depth of the glyph when drawn in 3D. This is an extrusion of the characters of the text in the Z axis.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the baseline of the text geometry should be expanded in the same manner as the existing geometry if the text extends beyond the baseline.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMTextSymbol.FlipAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the angle (in degrees from vertical) at which point rotated text is flipped (mirrored) in place.

member.summary: Gets or sets whether the text is drawn as subscript or superscript.

member.summary: Gets or sets the font encoding.

member.summary: Gets or sets the style name for the font family. e.g. Regular, Bold, or Italic.

member.summary: Gets or sets the type of font that the font family/style name reference.

member.summary: Gets or sets an array of CIM font variation objects, describing a particular instance of a variable font through the font axis tags and their values. The number of CIM font variations will correspond to the number of variation axes specified by the font. This is only used for variable fonts.

member.summary: Gets or sets an additional rotation that is applied to the individual glyphs contained in the text. This is applied to the individual glyphs whereas Angle, AngleX and AngleY are affect how the entire text string is oriented.

member.summary: Gets or sets the polygon symbol that is used to draw the halo for a text symbol.

member.summary: Gets or sets the size of the text in points.

member.summary: Gets or sets if hinting from the font is used for text rendering. Hinting is information included with most fonts to effectively fit the vector glyphs of the font into the raster grid onto which they are displayed.

member.summary: Gets or sets the alignment type used to align the text to the geometry horizontally. Affects which side of a point geometry the point text is drawn or which end of a line it is drawn close to. Commonly used to define how stacked text appears.

member.summary: Gets or sets how many points to indent the text from the beginning of the baseline for the first line only.

member.summary: Gets or sets the mass color substitute. When using the SymbolSubstitutionColor substitution type this is the color that all text graphics will be overridden with.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMAnnotationLayer.InlineColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the in-line color. When using the SymbolSubstitutionIndividualSubordinate or SymbolSubstitutionIndividualDominant substitution types this is the color that all text graphics that are stored in-line (bloated) will be overridden with.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMAnnotationLayer.SubstitutionSymbolCollection
member.summary: Gets or sets a symbol substitution collection.

remarks.para: When using the SymbolSubstitutionIndividualSubordinate or SymbolSubstitutionIndividualDominant substitution types this collection defines which symbols in the symbol collection are substituted and what their substitute values are.

The symbol substitution properties allow the users to swap out symbols/colors of annotation stored in the geodatabase at the layer level. This allows annotation to be re-purposed in maps without duplicating the annotation. The classic case for this behavior is when a user wishes to utilize black text generated for standard parcel maps on top of a map with raster imagery. By substituting the color or symbol collection of the annotation the user is allowed to change the appearance for this one map without a large performance or data management overhead.

One complex aspect of symbol substitution is how overrides are treated when it is enabled. When this feature was originally added some wanted overrides to be respected and others did not, so options were added for this (dominant and subordinate substitution types). When the dominant type is chosen overrides are ignored. When the subordinate type is chosen overrides are applied on top of the new symbols.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMAnnotationLayer.SubLayers
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of AnnotationSubLayers, corresponding to the annotation subclasses defined by the annotation feature class.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMDisplayTable
member.summary: Represents a display table.
member.remarks: A display table represents a virtual view of one or more tables. The display table always has a base table, but one or more tables can be joined and/or related to the base table. A join effectively adds new columns onto the base table, based on the foreign key to the joined table. A relate simply sets up an in-memory relationship class to another table to lookup related rows from a foreign key in the base table. The display table also supports a definition expression and allows the user to specify a 'display field', whose value is a label used to represent a row in the table.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMFeatureLayer
member.summary: Represents a layer that draws data from feature classes.

remarks.para: A feature layer displays a set of geographic features.

A geographic feature represents a real-world object on the earth. It has a spatially-referenced location, stored as a point, line, or polygon, and a set of attributes that describe the feature. Its position is accurate and relevant within a particular scale range. Geographic features are the core spatial data holdings of an organization. They can serve as official records, are used in spatial analysis, and are used as source data for cartography.

Feature layers draw their features by using a feature renderer to transform the geographic feature into one or more graphic entities. Feature renderers read the feature's geometry and attribute values to generate graphic entities that graphically depict the feature on a map.
