member.summary: Gets or sets the area symbolization type. This controls the line symbol style for area boundaries.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ColorScheme
member.summary: Gets or sets the color scheme.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowDataQuality
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display data quality (M_QUAL) for S-57 features.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.DeepContour
member.summary: Gets or sets the deep water contour depth in meters.
member.remarks: This must be greater than or equal to the safety contour value. When four(rather than two) depth shades are used, this controls the boundary between safe and deep areas.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowDisplayBase
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the S-52 "displaybase" display category is enabled.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowOtherDisplay
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the S-52 "other" display category is enabled.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowStandardDisplay
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the S-52 "standard" display category is enabled.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.DepthDisplayUnits
member.summary: Gets or sets the depth units (meters/feet/fathoms) for display.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowNOBJNM
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display the national name attribute on S-57 features.
member.remarks: This is text group 31 per IHO S-52 Annex A.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.HonorSCAMIN
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the 'SCAMIN' (scale min) S-57 feature attribute will be used.
member.remarks: If disabled, all ENC features will be rendered regardless of scale.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowIsolatedDangers
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display isolated dangers in shallow water.
member.remarks: This is viewing group 24020, 24050 per IHO 2-52 Annex A.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.LabelContours
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display the depth contour labels, including safety contour labels.
member.remarks: This is viewing group 33021, 33022 per IHO S-52 Annex A.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.LabelSafetyContours
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display the safety contour labels.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.ShowLowAccuracy
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use low accuracy symbols (CATZOC).
member.remarks: This is viewing group 31010 per IHO S-52 Annex A. When low accuracy is set to false, low accuracy data will be visually indistinguishable from other data.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.PointSymbolizationType
member.summary: Gets or sets the S-52 point feature symbolization type (simplified/paperchart).
member.remarks: Paperchart symbolization is based on traditional paper charts. Simplified symbols are more compact and visible.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMS52MarinerSettings.SafetyContour

member.summary: Gets or sets the depth of the shallow contour in meters.
member.remarks: This must be less than or equal to the safety contour value. When four(rather than two) depth shades are used, this value controls the separation between shallow and unsafe areas.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.CIMVectorTileLayer
member.summary: Represents a VectorTile layer.

remarks.para: A VectorTileServiceLayer provides rich cartographic content in a fast and efficient vector tile format. It may have multiple styles and if so users can choose which style to use to display the layer's vector geometries.

Logically a VectorTileServiceLayer is more like a basemap layer in that it is typically composed of several distinct data sources (e.g. roads, cities, hydrology, buildings) that can provide context and background but in a way that is typically more performant than raster tile layers.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType
member.summary: Problem types for the Location-Allocation solver

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMinimizeWeightedImpedance
member.summary: Chooses N facilities that will minimize the sum of weighted costs between the facilities and demand points (PMedian).

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMaximizeCoverage
member.summary: Chooses N facilities that will reach all demand points within a specified cutoff. Once all demand points have been reached the sum of weighted costs between the facilities and demand points will be minimized.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMaximizeCoverageMinimizeFacilities
member.summary: Chooses the minimum number of facilities necessary to reach all demand points. Solution facilities will minimize the sum of weighted costs between the facilities and demand points.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMaximizeAttendance
member.summary: Chooses N facilities that will maximize the demand point weight allocated to the facilities assuming that the allocated demand weight decreases with increased network distance.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMaximizeMarketShare
member.summary: Chooses N facilities that will maximize the market share of weighted demand points assuming the presence of competitor facilities. Uses a Huff model.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTTargetMarketShare
member.summary: Chooses the minimum number of facilities necessary to achieve the target marketshare of weighted demand points assuming the presence of competitor facilities. Uses a Huff model.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.CIM.esriNALocationAllocationProblemType.esriNALAPTMaximizeCapacitatedCoverage
member.summary: Chooses N facilities that will reach all demand points within a specified cutoff and subject to a per facility capacity constraint. The sum of weighted costs between the facilities and demand points will also be minimized.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.LasDataset.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.LasDataset.EstimatePointSpacing(ArcGIS.Core.Geometry.Envelope)
member.summary: Gets the minimum, maximum, and mean point spacing estimates based on the LAS files whose extents intersect the envelope. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: If only one file is within the extent then the minimum, maximum, and mean values will be the same. If multiple files are intersected the minimum is set to the file with the smallest spacing, maximum to the one with the largest, and mean is based on estimating the total points within the envelope. Point spacing estimates at this level (i.e., the dataset) are based on estimates made per LAS file. They'll be more reliable if statistics for the LAS dataset have been calculated.
member.param: The envelope. It will be projected into the spatial reference of the LAS dataset.
member.returns: The minimum, maximum and mean point spacing.
member.exception: cannot be null.

member.summary: Gets the return number of the point. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: The return number is the pulse return number for a given output pulse. A given output laser pulse can have many returns and they must be marked in sequence of return.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.LasPoint.ScanDirectionFlag
member.summary: Gets the scan direction flag of this point. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: The scan direction flag denotes the direction at which the scanner mirror was traveling at the time of the output pulse. A value of 1 is a positive scan direction (moving from the left side of the in-track direction to the right side) and a value of 0 is a negative scan direction.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.LasPoint.ScanAngleRank
member.summary: Gets the scan angle rank of this point. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: The scan angle rank is the angle (rounded to the nearest integer) at which the laser point was output from the laser system including the roll of the aircraft. The scan angle is within 1 degree of accuracy from +90 to -90 degrees.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.LasPoint.ScanAngleDegree
member.summary: Gets the scan angle of this point in degrees. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: The scan angle represents the rotational position of the emitted laser pulse with respect to the vertical of the coordinate system of the data. Each increment represents 0.006 degrees.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.Terrain
member.summary: Represents a terrain dataset.
member.remarks:
A terrain is a multiresolution, TIN-based surface built from measurements stored as features in a geodatabase. They're typically made from lidar, sonar, and photogrammetric sources. Terrains have participating feature classes and rules. See .
Terrain data is organized for fast retrieval. This organization involves the creation of terrain pyramids that are used to quickly retrieve only the data necessary to construct a surface of the required level of detail (LOD) for a given area of interest (AOI) from the database. See .

member.remarks:
TIN elements can exist "inside" or "outside" the TIN's data area. When TINs are initially built the only elements that are "outside" are the four super nodes and their incident edges and triangles. If clip or erase polygons are added to a TIN, they further modify what is considered to be "inside" or "outside".

member.summary: A is one of the three basic elements of a TIN. Edges are comprised of two TinNodes. Edges are oriented in clockwise order and are used to form triangles.
member.remarks: Edges may be hard, soft, or regular. Hard and soft edges are enforced in the triangulation. When a TIN is used as a surface model, these usually represent breaklines. Regular edges are simply a consequence of triangulation and don't have special meaning. The enumeration describes edge type.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinEdge.GetNextCounterClockwiseEdge
member.summary: Gets the edge terminating at the "fromNode" of this TIN edge. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: Returns the next edge, in a neighboring triangle, that is counter-clockwise to this edge relative to its from node. Consider the from node the center hub of a bicycle wheel and edges incident to it spokes. GetNextCounterClockwiseEdge returns the next spoke (edge) counter-clockwise. This member is useful when you need to circle around nodes. If the from node of an edge is one of the TIN's super nodes, GetNextCounterClockwiseEdge will return null when there is no next edge due to the fact the absolute boundary has been reached.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinEditor.#ctor(ArcGIS.Core.Geometry.Envelope)
member.summary: Creates a new TIN editor instance. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.param: The intended 2-dimensional domain of the TIN. Data subsequently added to the TIN should fall within this extent. If the envelope has a spatial reference, it will be copied and assigned to the TIN.
member.returns: The newly created TIN editor in edit mode.
member.remarks: The newly created tin editor is in edit mode. Four software synthesized nodes (called super nodes) will be used to form an initial triangulation. These will be positioned outside the declared extent. You should be fairly accurate with the extent so the positions of the super nodes is estimated correctly. Providing an unnecessarily large extent would result in the nodes being placed farther away than necessary from the data which can hurt performance and increase the likelihood of precision related issues.
member.exception: The envelope is null.
The envelope is empty.
This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.

example.code: tinEditor = new TinEditor(envelope); bool isInEditMode = tinEditor.IsInEditMode; // isInEditMode = true

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinEditor.CreateFromFeatureClass(ArcGIS.Core.Data.FeatureClass,ArcGIS.Core.Data.QueryFilter,ArcGIS.Core.Data.Field,ArcGIS.Core.Data.Field,ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinSurfaceType)
member.summary: Creates a new TIN editor instance. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.param: The feature class that provides the input geometries from which to create the TIN.
The filter that may be used to select a subset of features. This can be null. If it is null, then all the geometries in the feature class are used.

A field in the feature class that indicates where the heights for the shapes come from. If the shape geometry is 3D, and that's what you want to use, pass the shape field. Otherwise, a numeric field can be used.

A numeric field in the feature class used to assign tags to corresponding elements in the TIN. Tag values are integers that are assigned to nodes, edges, or triangles. They have user defined meaning (e.g. node accuracy, land cover, etc.). If no tag values are to be used pass null.
A surface type indicating how the input feature geometry is incorporated into the triangulation.
member.returns: The newly created TIN editor in edit mode.
member.remarks:
The extent of the feature class is copied and used as the extent of the TIN.
If records containing NULL shapes or numeric fields with NULL Z values are encountered, the triangulation process will skip them and continue. If this happens, a is thrown with the message "One or more input features contain NULL Shape or field value." when it's finished. Therefore, all valid data in the feature class gets triangulated but a note is made, in the form of a specific error, to let the you know one or more records were skipped. You then have the choice of using the resulting TIN or not.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinEditor.SetToConstrainedDelaunay
member.summary: Sets the triangulation method to constrained Delaunay from this point forward. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks:
Once this has been set, breaklines will no longer be densified with Steiner points in order to ensure the triangulation conforms to Delaunay criteria. The benefit of having it constrained is you get a best fit match between input and output surface without the need to add densification points. The drawback is the natural neighbors interpolator can't be used on a constrained TIN.
Once a TIN has been placed in this mode it cannot be changed back by any means other than not saving the edit session used to call this method.
member.exception: This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
The editor is not in edit mode.

example.code: // Set the triangulation method to constrained Delaunay from this point forward tinEditor.SetToConstrainedDelaunay();

member.summary: Adds features from a feature class to the TIN. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.param: The feature class that provides the input geometries from which to create the TIN.
The filter that may be used to select a subset of features. This can be null. If it is null, then all the geometries in the feature class are used.

A field in the feature class that indicates where the heights for the shapes come from. If the shape geometry is 3D, and that's what you want to use, pass the shape field. Otherwise, a numeric field can be used. If the heights for the features should be interpolated from the existing state of the TIN, assuming some features with heights had been previously added, you can pass null to indicate the features do not have Z values of their own.

A numeric field in the feature class used to assign tags to corresponding elements in the TIN. Tag values are integers that are assigned to nodes, edges, or triangles. They have user defined meaning (e.g. node accuracy, land cover, etc.). If no tag values are to be used, then pass null.
A surface type indicating how the input feature geometry is incorporated into the triangulation.
member.remarks: If records containing NULL shapes or numeric fields with NULL Z values are encountered, the triangulation process will skip them and continue. If this happens, a is thrown with the message "One or more input features contain NULL Shape or field value." when it's finished. Therefore, all valid data in the feature class gets triangulated but a note is made, in the form of a specific error, to let the you know one or more records were skipped. You then have the choice of using the resulting TIN or not.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinFilter.DataElementsOnly
member.summary: Gets and sets whether the filter should return elements classified as "inside" only. Default value is false.
member.remarks:
TIN elements can exist "inside" or "outside" the TIN's data area. When TINs are initially built the only elements that are "outside" are the four super nodes and their incident edges and triangles. If clip or erase polygons are added to a TIN, they further modify what is considered to be "inside" or "outside".
Use this property in conjunction with the and the properties to determine the elements retrieved.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinFilter.FilterType
member.summary: Gets and sets the filter type. Default value is .
member.remarks:
Use this property in conjunction with the and properties to determine the elements retrieved.
Here is a brief explanation of the possible combinations between and .
FilterType = All and DataElementsOnly = false; find all elements in the extent. If your extent is the super node extent (see ) or includes part of the super node extent, then super nodes and the incident edges and triangles will be retrieved.
FilterType = All and DataElementsOnly = true; find all elements in the extent that are classified as "inside". If your extent is the super node extent (see ) or includes part of the super node extent, then super nodes and the incident edges and triangles will not be retrieved as they are not classified as "inside".
FilterType = InsideTin and DataElementsOnly = false; find all elements inside the TIN not associated with super nodes that are in the extent.
FilterType = InsideTin and DataElementsOnly = true; find all elements inside the TIN not associated with super nodes that are in the extent and classified as "inside"
FilterType = InsideDataArea; find all elements inside the TIN's data area that are in the extent. Elements that are in the TIN's data area are by definition classified as "inside" so the DataElementsOnly property is unnecessary.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Analyst3D.TinFilter.FilterEnvelope
member.summary: Gets and sets an envelope filter. Default value is null meaning that the envelope searched is the TIN's data area, See .
member.remarks: Use this to specify a specific area to search rather than the TIN's data area. If specified, the envelope will be projected into the spatial reference of the TIN dataset.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.AttributedRelationshipClass
member.summary: Represents an association between two tables in a geodatabase on which additional information is stored in an intermediate table.
member.remarks: By default, the intermediate table has three system-generated fields whose name can be retrieved using , , , respectively. However, the intermediate table may have additional user-defined attributes defined at the moment the AttributedRelationshipClass is created. An AttributedRelationshipClass is always created for relationship classes whose cardinality is many-to-many () regardless of whether they have additional user-defined attributes.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.AttributedRelationshipClass.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.param: A handle to an underlying ArcObjects relationship class Data Element instance.
The datastore that contains the AttributedRelationshipClass dataset and its associated AttributedRelationshipClassDefinition.

Indicates if is a full definition. An AttributedRelationshipClassDefinition object obtained from its associated Dataset is considered a full definition (i.e., via AttributedRelationshipClass.Definition property). However, if a AttributedRelationshipClassDefinition is obtained directly from the via some kind of catalog scheme (assuming such a catalog scheme is supported by the workspace in question) for optimization reasons, it may *not* be a full definition. A non-full definition may render certain properties (e.g., ) unavailable (i.e., GetFields() always returns a count of 0). If there is any doubt as to whether is a full definition, just use the default false value. If false is specified and when the properties that require a full definition to be in place to work properly are invoked, this object will create a full definition on demand to ensure the behavior is always correct.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.AttributedRelationshipClassDefinition.EnsureFullDefinitionHasBeenCreated
member.summary: The reason it is important to make sure this definition's associated handle is a "full definition" is that when a definition is retrieved from a geodatabase catalog, certain important properties get left out such as the fields of a table/feature class. To get the fields, it is necessary to open the dataset first. To compromise between efficiency and correctness (getting a definition from a catalog is much more efficient), a "lazy" approach is used. In other words, the first time the Fields or FindField method is called, the "full definition" handle is retrieved. Subsequently, this same handle is used for as long as this object remains alive.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Database
member.summary: Represents the gateway to connect to a relational database, which may or may not be a geodatabase (please see remarks). Given a specific object, the Database data store can be used to open a single database table, or a query layer that is created from one or more database tables.
member.remarks: Although the Database data store can be used to access a geodatabase, this practice is not recommended. Instead, should be used instead. The main reason is that internally, the implementation of a Geodatabase table is different from that of a Database. There are certain operations in this class that require the table to be originally opened from a Database. If this precondition is not met, there will be a runtime exception ().

member.summary: Calculates the extent for the spatial single table or query layer specified by . This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.param: The extent of the feature class that needs to be calculated.
member.remarks: When a spatial table (i.e., FeatureClass) or its corresponding definition (i.e., FeatureClassDefinition) is first opened, the FeatureClass object's extent is set to the domain of its spatial reference (i.e., the XMin, YMin, XMax, YMax of the spatial reference's extent). The reason is that depending on the size of a database table, it can be expensive to calculate all the geometries to accurately find the envelope. Thus, if clients truly want to find the accurate extent of a specific feature class, they can do so by calling this method.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Dataset.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.summary: Represents a mechanism to create a . See also .
member.remarks:
There are a number of different constructor overloads provided allowing an entity type description to be initialized from a number of different sources including:
A table or feature class definition.
A .
Another KnowledgeGraphRelationshipTypeDescription.
A collection of .
Various other overloads that also include a name and spatial column ("shape description").
Note: A spatial column for both KnowledgeGraphEntityTypes and KnowledgeGraphRelationshipTypes is optional. KnowledgeGraphEntityTypes and KnowledgeGraphRelationshipTypes created with a shape column will be represented as feature classes in the knowledge graph geodatabase and KnowledgeGraphEntityTypes and KnowledgeGraphRelationshipTypes created without a shape column will be represented as tables.
When initializing a KnowledgeGraphEntityTypeDescription, an ObjectID and GlobalID KnowledgeGraphPropertyDescription will automatically be added to the list of property descriptions (if they were not provided as inputs to the relevant constructor) within the . In the case of the relationship type, the underlying origin and destination entity id fields will also be automatically be added to the list of property descriptions within the

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.DDL.SchemaBuilder.Build
member.summary: Performs all enqueued operations. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks:
If an edit session is in progress on the specified geodatabase or knowledge graph an InvalidOperationException will be thrown.
When using the Pro SDK Add-In-based DDL, do not perform DDL operations while the dataset is open in the map. Remove the dataset before making changes, and add it back after completing the operation.
If executing schema operations on a knowledge graph from within an Add-In, to ensure proper refresh of the application UI, schema builder operations should be executed within a call to knowledgeGraph.ApplySchemaEdits(sb) where the knowledge graph is the same knowledge graph used initialize the schema builder via its constructor. Calling schemaBuilder.Build() directly when it has been constructed with a knowledge graph may result in the application UI not refreshing correctly. Additionally, calling knowledgeGraph.ApplySchemaEdits(sb) when the schema builder was initialized with a geodatabase (not a knowledge graph) will result in an InvalidOperationException.
Currently, the following operations are supported for knowledge graphs:
o Create (named object types and attribute index)
o Delete named object types
o Modify*
*Refer to for specific details on what modifications can be made to knowledge graph named object type schemas.
member.returns: True ,if all operations ran successfully; otherwise False. Any returned errors and error messages can be accessed in

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.FeatureDataset.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Field
member.summary: Represents a column in a table.

remarks.para: Provides access to members that return information about the field. The field object represents a column in a table. A field has many properties, the most obvious ones being its name and its data type. The enumeration lists the possible datatypes.

Some field names, although valid in ArcGIS, conflict with internal properties used by Enterprise geodatabases for storing geometries. A table created using one of these field names will have the field name qualified in the table to avoid potential ambiguity. A qualified field name is returned as "USERNAME.TABLENAME.FIELDNAME" by Oracle and "DATABASE.USERNAME.TABLENAME.FIELDNAME" by SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

The following 14 field names will be qualified in Enterprise geodatabases: FID, AREA, LEN, POINTS, NUMOFPTS, ENTITY, EMINX, EMINY, EMAXX, EMAXY, EMINZ, EMAXZ, MIN_MEASURE and MAX_MEASURE. The property of these fields will be qualified when retrieved from the datasets fields collection. Attempting to retrieve the index of a qualified field using requires the developer to qualify the field name.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.GeodatabaseCore.CreateExactManagedWrapperNoThrowFor(System.IntPtr,ArcGIS.Core.Data.DatasetType)
member.summary: Wraps the native definition handle in its exact corresponding managed class. For example, if is RelationshipClass, but the actual type of the native handle is attributed relationship class, because of the mismatch, the native handle will not be wrapped and null is returned. However, if both and the type of the native handle is non-attributed RelationshipClass (in other words, the exact same type), a wrapped instance of RelationshipClassDefinition is returned.
member.param: The handle to the native definition object.
The dataset type of the definition handle.
member.returns: A specific managed wrapper class that corresponds to the type of the native handle. Otherwise, null is returned.
member.remarks: The difference between this method and is that for relationship classes, if is RelationshipClass, but the actual definition handle is attributed relationship class, then no wrapper instance will be created and null is returned. By the same token, if is AttributedRelationshipClass, but the actual definition handle is relationship class, then null is returned. The exact wrapper instance is returned if and only if the matches exactly the type of the native handle.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Exceptions.ServiceExceptionUtil
member.summary: This utility class provides translation from a service-related COMException to or one of its derived type. This class is intended to be used by any managed class that interops with *service* related ArcObjects code (e.g., SystemCore\MessageConnection.cpp or code in the Server\GISClient library). More importantly, this class is built with a fallback mechanism in mind. If an HRESULT is not recognized to have originated from service-related ArcObjects components, this class with forward the translation request to , which acts as this API's primary as well as default exception-handling utility class.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Exceptions.ServiceExceptionUtil.TranslateException(System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException)
member.summary: Translates to a specific type of either or . if the is recognized to have originated from service-related ArcObjects components. Otherwise, the request is forwarded to .
member.param: A generic COMException that is thrown by the runtime when an HResult is returned from interop native code.
member.returns: An instance of with a meaningful message if the HRESULT is recognized to have originated from service-related ArcObjects components. Otherwise, the request is forwarded to .

members.member:
Available Service-related error codes as specified in MessageSupport.idl (from the System library, current as of version 1.2, 15 September 2015) and AGSClient.idl (from the GISClient libray, current as of version 1.1, 19 July 2013). Even though the error codes from these service-related libraries fall under their own categories, unlike the arrangement done for the error codes in the GeodatabaseExceptionUtil class, however, the error categories in this class (i.e., ServiceExceptionUtil) will not have their own corresponding GeodatabaseException-derived classes (e.g., AGSClientException). Instead, they will fall under ServiceException.
It is important to *update* this file when the aforementioned idl files have updated contents.
Category: AGS Client -- 0x0900 + 1 to 0x0900 + 6 Category: Message Support -- 0x0200 + 1 to 0x0200 + 32

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.SetOperation.Intersection
member.summary: All rows present in both input selections are copied to the output selection. Those row IDs present in only one set are discarded. This is a Boolean AND operation.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.SetOperation.SymmetricDifference
member.summary: All rows present in either input selection, but not present in both, are copied to the output selection. This is a Boolean XOR operation.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.SetOperation.Union
member.summary: All rows present in the first selection and the second selection are copied to the output selection. This is a Boolean OR operation.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.SpatialRelationship
member.summary: Specifies the spatial relationship.

list.item: Intersects - Returns a feature if any spatial relationship is found.
EnvelopeIntersects - Returns a feature if the envelope of the two shapes intersect.
Contains - Returns a feature if its shape is wholly contained within the search geometry. Valid of all shape type combinations.

Crosses - Returns a feature if the intersection of the interiors of the two shapes is not empty and has a lower dimension that the maximum dimension of the two shapes. Two lines that share an endpoint do not cross. Valid for polyline/polyline, polyline/Area, multipoint/Area, and multipoint/polyline shape type combinations.
IndexIntersects uses the underlying index grid of the target feature class which is faster than using the envelope of the features, and is often used to return features for display purposes.

Overlaps - Returns a feature if the intersection of the two shapes results in an object of the same dimension, but different from both of the shapes. Applies to Area/Area, polyline/polyline, and multipoint/multipoint shape type combinations.

Touches - Returns a feature if the two shapes share a common boundary. However, the intersection of the interiors of the two shapes must be empty. In the point/polyline case, the point may touch an endpoint only of the polyline. Applies to all combinations except for point/point.
Within - Returns a feature if its shape wholly contains the search geometry. Valid for all shape type combinations.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Knowledge.Analytics.KnowledgeGraphCentralityScores.Item(System.Object)
member.summary: Indexer to retrieve the array of scores for a specific entity identified by its UID.
member.remarks:
Returns the scores for the centrality computation for the input uid used as the key to the indexer. The returned array of scores contains one score, or "result", per input used in the centrality analysis. Scores are arranged in the array in the same order as the measures in the input measures array.
. Note: The uid is the entity object identifier (refer to )
member.returns: The array of centrality measure scores for the given entity

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Knowledge.Analytics.KnowledgeGraphCentralityScores.RawScores
member.summary: Gets the "raw" array of all scores for all entities used in the centrality analysis.
member.remarks:
Within the array, the scores are ordered by measure by entity. Use the following formula to do your own indexing into the array:
score = ([measure_index * entity_count] + entity_index)
Example: Assume you calculated 3 centrality measures across 1000 entities:
total number of scores = 3 * 1000 = 3000.
where:
measure_index = 0 for the first measure, 1 for the second measure, 2 for the third measure.
entity_count = 1000.
entity_index = index for the given entity uid in the array (i.e. the 0-based index of the uid in RawUids)
The first 1000 scores in the array will be the scores for the first measure, the second 1000 scores will be for the second measure and the third 1000 scores will be for the third measure.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Knowledge.Analytics.ResultPath
member.summary: Gets the representation of a single path returned by the Filtered Find Paths algorithm.
member.remarks:
The path is a sequence of relationships groups. Relationship groups that have more than one relationship contain "parallel" relationships, i.e relationships between the same two entities.
Refer to .
member.example:
If paths "(A) -[r1]-> (B) -[r2]-> (C)" and "(A) -[r1]-> (B) -[r3]-> (C)" are both valid, Filtered Find Paths will return a single path containing:
- a relationship group with r1
- a relationship group with r2 and r3.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Knowledge.Analytics.KnowledgeGraphSubGraphBuilder
member.summary: A builder for creating a for use in KnowledgeGraph operations such as centrality.
member.remarks:
This builder aids in building a from a . To build a more complex or use property filters (), create the and its component filters and manually.
The following are examples of what a CIMKnowledgeGraphSubGraph would look like given a Knowledge Graph with entity types (A, B, C, D).
Refer to defining the list of filters for entities, and defining whether a particular filter includes or excludes the instances it represents. Ordering of filters does not matter.
o When the collection of filters in the CIMKnowledgeGraphSubGraph is null, all entities are implicitly in the subgraph, i.e the resulting set of entities in the subgraph is {A, B, C, D}.
o When there is a single filter and it includes A, the resulting set of entities in the subgraph is {A}.
o When there is a single filter and it excludes A, the resulting set of entities in the subgraph is {B, C, D}.
o When there are two filters, one filter includes A and one filter excludes B, the resulting set of entities in the subgraph is still {A}. (i.e. B, C, and D are all excluded, the "exclusion" filter was unnecessary in this case as only A was explicitly included)
To include or exclude just a specific subset of entities within a given entity type, use either or .
The filtering behaviors described above for entities apply equally to relationships - which are configured in exactly the same way. Refer to .
Note: relationships having at least one entity endpoint that is not in the subgraph are also not in the subgraph.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.LinearReferencing.EventInfo
member.summary: Represents information for an event table. Each row in the table references an event, and its location is expressed as measurements along a route feature.
member.remarks: An event is a linear, continuous, or point feature that occurs along a route feature. Anything that occurs on or describes a route feature can be an event. There are two types of events: point events and line events. A point event describes a discrete location along a route (a point), whereas a line event describes a portion of a route (a line).

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.LinearReferencing.RouteEventSource
member.summary: Represents a dynamic feature class created through the dynamic segmentation process.

remarks.para: Dynamic segmentation is the process of computing the map location (shape) of events stored in an event table.
The shapes of a route event source cannot be edited because they are generated by the dynamic segmentation process. When you edit a route event, you are editing the underlying event table.
Dynamic segmentation allows multiple sets of attributes to be associated with any portion of a linear feature.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.LinearReferencing.RouteInfo
member.summary: Represents a route feature class's information, . A route feature class is an M-enabled polyline feature class containing a unique identifier attribute field.
member.remarks: A route is any line feature, such as a street, highway, river, or pipe, that contains a unique identifier and a system of measurement. Routes are stored in an M-enabled feature class containing a unique identifier attribute field. The M-values are used to measure the distance along a line feature. Measures can be any unit of measurement, such as miles, meters, and time, and they are stored as M-values on route vertices.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Mapping.CatalogDataset
member.summary: Represents a catalog dataset. A catalog dataset is the container for item references, which are called catalog dataset items - not unlike raster references stored in a raster catalog
member.remarks:
Catalog datasets function similarly to polygon feature classes, with some essential differences. When viewing the dataset's attribute table, each record is an item in the catalog dataset containing a reference to its data path. The Shape field includes the footprint geometry for each item. This means that all catalog dataset items must have a spatial geometry — you cannot add tables or table web layers to catalog datasets.
The footprint envelopes all of the item's features, rasters, and so forth. Each footprint feature's attributes are properties specific to the purpose, scope, and validation status of each dataset item.You can add, update, and maintain your own fields and values in the dataset's attribute table, and establish a join or relate with other tables, but you cannot access or edit the attribute table of the containing footprint layer.

The datastore that contains the FeatureClass dataset and its associated FeatureClassDefinition.

Indicates if is a full definition. A FeatureClassDefinition object obtained from its associated FeatureClass Dataset is considered a full definition (i.e., via FeatureClass.GetDefinition()). However, if a FeatureClassDefinition is obtained directly from the via some kind of catalog scheme (assuming such a catalog scheme is supported by the workspace in question) for optimization reasons, it may *not* be a full definition. A non-full definition may render certain properties (e.g., ) unavailable (i.e., the GetFields() always returns a count of 0). If there is any doubt as to whether is a full definition, just pass in false. If false is specified and when the properties that require a full definition to be in place to work properly are invoked, this object will create a full definition on demand to ensure the behavior is always correct.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Angle Directed diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm moves a diagram's edges in specified alignment directions.
member.remarks: This layout algorithm progressively moves the diagram's edges in specified alignment directions. For each diagram edge, this layout considers its current direction, searches for the nearest desired direction among those specified, and moves the edge in that direction.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Directions
member.summary: The number of directions that must be used to align the diagram edges and their connected junctions

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Directions.FourDirections
member.summary: Four directions. The edges will move so they progressively approach one of the 4 axes, starting with the edge's origin junction and inclined at 90, 180, 270, or 360 degrees.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Directions.EightDirections
member.summary: Eight directions. The edges will move so they progressively approach one of the 8 axes, starting with the edge's origin junction and inclined at 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315, or 360 degrees.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Directions.TwelveDirections
member.summary: Twelve directions. The edges will move so they progressively approach one of the 12 axes, starting with the edge's origin junction and inclined at 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240, 270, 300, 330, or 360 degrees.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.#ctor
member.summary: Constructor of the angle directed diagram layout parameters class.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.NumberOfIterations
member.summary: Gets and sets the number of iterations used when computing the layout.
member.remarks: The default value is 1.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.PreserveContainers
member.summary: Indicates whether or not the containers are preserved.

ul.li: If true, the layout algorithm executes on the top graph of the diagram so that containers are preserved.
If false, the layout algorithm executes on both content and non-content features in the diagram. The default is false.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.AngleDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.NumberOfDirections
member.summary: The number of directions that must be used to align the diagram edges and their connected junctions.
member.remarks: The default is .

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Compression diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm compresses the diagram features toward the middle of the diagram.
member.remarks: This algorithm is useful for networks that span thousands of miles and are otherwise difficult to view and understand in their true geographic positions—for example, in the transmission utilities industry.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.VertexRule
member.summary: Determines how vertices along edges in the diagram must be processed.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.VertexRule.AllVertices
member.summary: All vertices on all edges will be removed from the diagram

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.VertexRule.AllOuterVertices
member.summary: All outer vertices are removed. Any edge vertices that are within the detected junctions' groups will be maintained, while edge vertices that are outside will be removed. When there are containers in the diagram that have edges that intersect the container polygons, a vertex is added at the intersection of the edge and container polygon.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.VertexRule.AllOuterVerticesExceptTheFirstOne
member.summary: All outer vertices except the first one are removed. Any edge vertices that are within the detected junctions' groups will be maintained, while edge vertices that are outside will be removed. When there are containers in the diagram that have edges that intersect the container polygons, the first (or last) outside vertex is preserved on edges that intersect a container polygon. A vertex is automatically inserted at the intersection of the edges and container polygons.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.#ctor
member.summary: Constructor of the compression diagram layout parameters class.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.MaxDistanceForGrouping
member.summary: Gets and sets the maximum distance for grouping.
member.remarks: The grouping distance is used to determine whether two connected junctions are close enough to be considered part of the same junctions group. A junctions group represents many junctions that are moved as a group during execution. The group may contain both junctions and containers. To group two junctions together, they must also be connected in the diagram by an edge. The default is 20 units in the diagram's coordinate system.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.PreserveContainers
member.summary: Indicates whether or not the containers are preserved.

ul.li: If true, the layout algorithm executes on the top graph of the diagram so that containers are preserved. The default is true.
If false, the layout algorithm executes on both content and non-content features in the diagram.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.CompressionDiagramLayoutParameters.VertexRemovalRule
member.summary: Gets and sets the vertex removal rule.
member.remarks: The default is .

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Force Directed diagram layout parameters.
member.remarks:
This layout algorithm uses a physical analogy to draw graphs by considering a graph a force system in which it tries to locally minimize the energy. It searches for an equilibrium state of the force system—a position for each diagram junction where the total force on each junction is zero.
Because this algorithm has a tendency to emphasize loops contained in a network diagram, it is often used by operators who manage highly meshed networks, such as water, wastewater, or gas.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Freedom
member.summary: Factor that limits the area used to move the diagram junctions during each algorithm iteration.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Freedom.Low
member.summary: Low degree of freedom. The area used to move the diagram junctions will be very limited.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Freedom.Medium
member.summary: Medium degree of freedom. The area used to move the diagram junctions will be moderate.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.Freedom.High
member.summary: High degree of freedom. The area used to move the diagram junctions will be very large.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.EdgeType
member.summary: The type of display for the diagram edges.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.EdgeType.Regular
member.summary: Regular. All diagram edges display as straight lines.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.EdgeType.Orthogonal
member.summary: Orthogonal.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.EdgeType.Curved
member.summary: Curved. All diagram edges are curved.

member.summary: Gets and sets the number of iterations used when computing the layout.
member.remarks: The default is 20.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ForceDirectedDiagramLayoutParameters.PreserveContainers

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.GridDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Grid diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm positions diagram junctions relative to a predefined magnetic grid.

ul.li: This algorithm positions diagram junctions relative to a magnetic grid that has cell sizes fixed by the and parameter values.

A grid with a specified cell size is essentially placed on the top of the diagram. The algorithm controls the number of cells that comprise a grid. This is calculated by factoring in the number of junctions that are going to be placed in the grid and the number of junctions that belong to each cell in the virtual grid.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.LinearDispatchDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Linear Dispatch diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithms spaces out diagram junctions that are visually too close, overlapping, or coincident.

ul.li: This layout algorithm spaces out diagram junctions that are visually too close, overlapping, or coincident. It moves junctions along their connected edges. The movement along the edges depends on the current and relative position of junctions and on the layout parameters.

This algorithm also separates diagram edges connected to the target junctions. The valence for these junctions is taken into account—that is, the number of their adjacent edges as well as the edge paths can be preserved.
This layout is especially useful for water, wastewater, and gas but can be deployed for other industries as well.

member.summary: User defined distance. All junctions with two connected edges will move so there is a minimum distance () between them and the other end of the edges they connect to. This occurs at the end of the layout execution.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.PartialOverlappingEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Partial Overlapping Edges diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm spaces out collinear edges or collinear portions of edges (edge segments) inside a given buffer zone.

ul.li: This layout algorithm detects sets of collinear edges or collinear portions of edges (edge segments) that can be considered as being inside a buffer zone of a given size.

The edges or segments must be relatively close to each other—more or less parallel, overlap, or nearly overlap—and similar in length. Segment buffer zones are then repositioned equally on the left and right sides, a proportional distance from the middle of the zone.

The distance between each segment is equal to a given offset. If vertices exist along diagram edges, the global orientation of the segments is preserved as much as possible. This is done so that, for example, a segment lying on the left side of another segment still ends up on the left side.

member.summary: Constructor of the partial overlapping edges layout parameters class.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.PartialOverlappingEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.OptimizeEdges
member.summary: Indicates if the segment placement order in each set of detected collinear segments are optimized to try to avoid crossing.

ul.li: If true, the placement of segments is optimized in each set of collinear segments. This is done by focusing on their connections instead of their positions. Segments that cross each other can be repositioned so they do not cross.
If false, the initial position of each segment is maintained in the collinear segment set and crossings are preserved. This is the default option.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.SmartTreeDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Smart Tree diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm arranges diagram features hierarchically and places them in a smart tree.
member.remarks:
This layout algorithm arranges the diagram features hierarchically and places them in a smart tree according to the direction and spacing distances specified.
When a root junction is specified in the diagram, the Smart Tree Layout algorithm builds a smart tree starting from that junction.
When several root junctions are specified in the diagram, those root junctions are aligned along the same axis perpendicularly to the tree direction and appear as different start points for a tree branch of the diagram.
If no root junction is specified, the algorithm selects the diagram junction associated with the smallest utility network topology index and considers this junction the root junction.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RotateTreeDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Rotate Tree diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm rotates the tree or trees related to pivot junctions currently set up in a diagram to the specified angle.

ul.li: This layout algorithm rotates the tree or trees related to the pivot junctions currently set up in the input network diagram layer according to the specified angle.

The Rotate Tree algorithm requires at least one pivot junction, such as a junction used as the center point around which the related graph will be rotated. The Rotate Tree layout also takes into account any barriers in the input diagram layer to prevent the algorithm from executing beyond the barriers.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Reshape Diagram Edges diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm processes simple operations on vertices along edges.
member.remarks: This layout is used to process simple operations on vertices along edges in network diagrams. It enables you to reduce all vertices or some vertices along diagram edges, square diagram edges with the addition of vertices on edges, and separate diagram edges that overlap.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation
member.summary: The type of reshape operation.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation.SquareEdges
member.summary: Square edges operation. Inserts vertices along diagram edges so these edges are displayed with right angles.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation.RemoveVertices
member.summary: Remove vertices operation. Removes all vertices along any edges in the diagram.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation.SeparateOverlappingEdges
member.summary: Separate overlapping edges operation. Separates edges that connect the same origin and extremity junctions when they are overlapping.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation.ReduceVerticesByAngle
member.summary: Reduce vertices by angle operation. Removes some or all vertices displayed along diagram edges according to the angle that separates the segments incident to those vertices.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.Operation.MarkCrossingEdges
member.summary: Mark crossing edges operation. Inserts circle arcs along diagram edges to mark the crossing with other edges.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkPosition
member.summary: The type of mark crossing position.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkPosition.MarkCrossingLeft
member.summary: The circular arc is on the left of the vertical segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkPosition.MarkCrossingRight
member.summary: The circular arc is on the right of the vertical segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkPosition.MarkCrossingAbove
member.summary: The circular arc is above the horizontal segment.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkPosition.MarkCrossingBelow
member.summary: The circular arc is below the horizontal segment.

member.summary: Constructor of the reshape edges diagram layout parameters class.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.PreservePath
member.summary: Indicates whether or not the path is preserved if the equals .

ul.li: If true, all vertices along the connected edges will be kept, and new vertices will be added at the moved junctions' original location. This is the default.
If false, vertices along edges will not be preserved.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.PreserveContainers
member.summary: Indicates whether or not the containers are preserved.

ul.li: If true, the layout algorithm executes on the top graph of the diagram so that containers are preserved.
If false, the layout algorithm executes on both content and non-content features in the diagram. The default is false.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.ThresholdAngle
member.summary: Threshold angle when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The angle formed by the incident segments over which the vertex related to these segments is reduced. The wider the angle, the fewer vertices are reduced. The default is 160 degrees.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.EdgeSpacing
member.summary: Edge spacing when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The absolute spacing that will separate two edges. The default is 0.5 in the units of the diagram's coordinate system.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.SegmentSpacing
member.summary: Segment spacing when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The spacing that will separate parallel segments of squared edges incident to the same junction. The default is 5 in the units of the diagram's coordinate system.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.BreakpointSpacing
member.summary: Breakpoint spacing when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The maximum distance between each junction to the first or last break point along edges incident to that junction when those edges are squared. The default is 8.66 in the units of the diagram's coordinate system.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.ReshapeOperation
member.summary: Specifies how edges will be reshaped.
member.remarks: The default is .

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.CircularArcRadius
member.summary: Circular arc radius when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The radius of the circular arc used to mark the edges crossings. The default is 5.0 in the units of the diagram's coordinate system.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.ReshapeEdgesDiagramLayoutParameters.MarkCrossingPosition
member.summary: Specifies the position of the mark crossing when executing the operation.
member.remarks: The default is .

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.MainRingDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Main Ring diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm arranges the diagram features in a network diagram around a main ring.

ul.li: This layout algorithm arranges the diagram features around the main ring and hierarchically lays out the subset of diagram features that connect to each diagram junction placed along the main ring.
The main ring is the loop formed by the largest number of edges in the network diagram.
If the network diagram contains no loops, the Main Ring layout algorithm execution has no effect.
This layout algorithm is typically used in the telecommunications industry.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.MainRingDiagramLayoutParameters.MainRingType.Ellipse
member.summary: Ellipse. The diagram features of the detected main ring will display along an ellipse.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.MainRingDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeType.RightMainLine
member.summary: RightMainLine. Each tree will be displayed hierarchically along a main line, and its related branches will be arranged on the right side of this main line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.MainRingDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeType.MainLine
member.summary: MainLine. Each tree will be displayed along a main line, and its related branches will be arranged on both the left and right sides of this main line.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.MainRingDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeType.SmartTree

member.summary: Relative position (between 0 and 1) of the break point on the subtree edges.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters
member.summary: Represents the Relative Mainline diagram layout parameters. This layout algorithm arranges diagram junctions and edges along a relative main line.

ul.li: This layout algorithm arranges the network diagram features in the input network diagram along parallel straight lines for which all the connected edges have the same attribute value. It also places the branches coming from those lines, preserving both their directions regarding the straight lines and distances proportional to the initial distances and relative to each other.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeDirection
member.summary: The direction of the mainline

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeDirection.FromTopToBottom
member.summary: Top to bottom direction. The relative main line will be drawn as a vertical line starting from the top and ending at the bottom.

member.name: F:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.TreeDirection.FromLeftToRight
member.summary: Left to right direction. The relative main line will be drawn as a horizontal line starting from the left and ending on the right.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.#ctor
member.summary: Constructor of the main line tree diagram layout parameters class.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.CompressAlongDirection
member.summary: Indicates whether or not the compression along the main line direction is active.

ul.li: If true, the layout algorithm will reduce the distances between adjacent groups of neighbor junctions along the direction while trying to maintain relative positioning between these groups. Neighbor junctions are junctions that are geographically close to each other without being directly connected.
If false, no compression occurs. This is the default.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.MinimalDistance
member.summary: Minimal distance that must be kept between two adjacent groups of neighbor junctions.
member.remarks: This minimal distance is also used to group neighbor junctions regarding their projection along the direction axis. Two junctions projected on this axis will belong to the same group when the distance between the two projected points is lower than this distance. The default is 0.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.OffsetBetweenBranches
member.summary: The spacing between two adjacent branches along the axis perpendicular to the direction of the line.
member.remarks: The default is 2.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.BreakPointAngle
member.summary: The angle that will be used to position the break point on the branches.

ul.li: The angle is a number between 0 and 90 degrees which is combined with the OffsetBetweenBranches parameter value to compute the break point position. When the break point angle value is 90 degrees, each branch displays orthogonally. The default is 45.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.CompressionRatio
member.summary: Compression ratio used to compress the junction along the axis of the main line.
member.remarks: The compression is only used when the compression along the main line direction is activated. It is a number between 0 and 100 that is applied to the length of any edge after subtracting the minimal distance of its length. When it is 100, the distance between each detected junction group is equal to the minimal distance. The default is 0.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.Direction
member.summary: The direction of the relative main line.
member.remarks: The default is .

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.LineAttributeName
member.summary: The name of the network attribute that will be used to identify the lines which compose the straight lines.
member.remarks: This name must exist on the utility network line classes. The values should be the same for all the edges that compose a straight line.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.TypeAttributeName
member.summary: The name of the network attribute that is used to group lines into types.
member.remarks: This name may exist on the utility network line classes. Its values allow lines to be grouped into types.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.AlignmentAttributeName
member.summary: The name of the network attribute that will be used to align individual line features.
member.remarks: The algorithm takes lines with the same value and aligns them with one another.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.LengthAttributeName
member.summary: The network attribute that the layout algorithm uses to measure the length of the diagram edges.
member.remarks: This length determines the positions of the junctions along the direction. By default, without specifying this name, the distances between the connected junctions along the direction are computed with the current edge length and the length of the shortest edge. When the LengthAttributeName is specified, these distances are computed with the values of this attribute for each edge.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.MainlineValues
member.summary: The TypeAttributeName values that identify the main lines.
member.remarks: When such values exist, they must be the same for any edge that composes the main lines (which could come from multiple utility network feature classes).

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.BranchValues
member.summary: The TypeAttributeName values that identify the branches.

member.name: P:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.RelativeMainlineDiagramLayoutParameters.ExcludedValues
member.summary: The TypeAttributeName values that identify the edges that must be excluded from the straight lines; that is, crossovers or ladders.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.NetworkDiagrams.NetworkDiagram.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Parcels.ParcelFabric.#ctor
member.summary: The purpose of this parameterless (i.e., default) constructor is to facilitate the usage of the generic method ArcGIS.Core.Internal.Interop.CreateWrapperOnHandle<T>(IntPtr handle), which requires a default constructor for it to work. Note that said generic method is not used in the ArcGIS.Core.Data or ArcGIS.Core.Data-derived namespace. It is strictly used by other callers in the ArcGIS system. Because using this default constructor to create an object requires an additional step of explicitly calling Attach() on the newly created object with a valid IntPtr handle, it is best to avoid using this constructor. Instead, use the non-default constructor that requires explicit arguments to be passed in at construction time.

member.summary: Constructs a ParcelFabricDefinition object that holds the metadata and other properties of a ParcelFabric dataset.
member.param: A handle to an underlying ArcObjects ParcelFabric Data Element instance.
The datastore that contains the ParcelFabric dataset and its associated ParcelFabricDefinition.
The parcel fabric associated with this instance of definition. If it is not available at the time of creation, null should be passed in.

Indicates if is a full definition. A ParcelFabricDefinition object obtained from its associated ParcelFabric Dataset is considered a full definition (i.e., via ParcelFabric.GetDefinition()). However, if a ParcelFabricDefinition is obtained directly from the via some kind of catalog scheme (assuming such a catalog scheme is supported by the workspace in question) for optimization reasons, it may *not* be a full definition. For ParcelFabric, this may not be an issue. However, for some other datasets such as Table, a non-full definition may render certain properties (e.g., ) unavailable (i.e., the GetFields() always returns a count of 0). If there is any doubt as to whether is a full definition, just pass in false. If false is specified and when the properties/methods that require a full definition to be in place to work properly are invoked, this object will create a full definition on demand to ensure the behavior is always correct.

When a Plugin Datasource add-in is loaded into the system at runtime, the framework may instantiate multiple instances of the concrete PluginDatasourceTemplate implementation. In particular, when a plug-in data source with a specific is used to open a specific , the framework will create a new instance of this concrete implementation followed by calling this Open method. If there are pertinent data that must be reflected across all instances of this concrete implementation, e.g., if the value of depends on a given data source associated with the and if said value must be reflected across all instances in order for the framework to behave properly, then it is the responsibility of this concrete implementation to ensure the data are properly shared and/or updated.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Core.Data.QueryDescription.IsObjectIDMappedColumnRequired
member.summary: Indicates if a virtual ObjectID column is required. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.returns: true if a virtual ObjectID column is required; otherwise, false (please see remarks).

remarks.para: In order for a database table to behave normally, it needs to have an ObjectID column (or a column of some other name) whose type is either or AND that the type must be non-nullable. However, there are situations in which such a column does not exist. Consider the example of a query layer-based QueryDescription object whose does not include such a column in its selection list. In such a situation, in order for IsObjectIDMappedColumnRequired to be true, one of the following two cases must be true.
1) There is only one non-nullable field whose type is either , or .
2) There are more than one non-nullable fields whose type is either , , , or .

Furthermore, beware of IsObjectIDMappedColumnRequired returning false. If this method returns false AND returns an empty string, it is most likely the fields on the selection list in are either nullable and/or they are not of type , , , , or . When this situation occurs, calling will cause an exception unless is invoked first with one or more valid fields as arguments.

remarks.para: The subfield property requests a minimum set of fields to return values for, by restricting the set of fields for which values are returned you can optimize the performance of the query when using a query filter. Additional values may be returned for fields that the query requires (e.g., ObjectID or Shape fields). Fields not included in the subfields list or required by the query are still present in the rows returned, but are not populated with values. Including all of the fields in the row ensures that the field index position is constant no matter how it was hydrated.

The default setting for subfields is to request values to be returned for all fields. The strings of "*" or "" can be set to return the query to this default. The default of returning all fields should always be used if the intent of the operation is to alter the values of the row and store it.
To set the subfields property to request the values to be returned for the "Name" and "Age" fields a string of "Name, Age" should be provided (white space is optional).
It is not required to set the subfields property if the query filter is to be used in a context where no rows are returned (e.g., ).

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Core.Data.Raster.PixelBlock
member.summary: Represents a container for pixel data that can be created using
member.remarks: The PixelBlock object is designed to handle generic pixel arrays from any raster data source. This means it must be able to handle single and multiband data, as well as support different pixel types. To support multiple bands, or planes, of raster data, the PixelBlock provides a separate array for each band (plane) in the raster. You can get the pixel data from the pixel block, modify the pixel values, and write the pixel block with the modified pixel values to a raster band. If the pixel block is created from a Raster, the modified pixel block can be read using the method and written to the raster dataset using the method. For a small raster dataset, the size of the pixel block can be the size of the entire dataset, which can usually be held in memory at one time. When working with large raster data, the best practice is to divide the raster into small pixel blocks and read and write these block by block using the Object.

member.summary: Gets the NoData mask for the given plane from this pixel block. This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.remarks: Conceptually, a NoData mask is a two-dimensional array in which each element corresponds to a pixel in the raster. Each element can have a value of 1 or 0; 1 indicates the pixel is a value pixel and 0 means the pixel is NoData. In order to save space, the NoData mask is actually stored as a one-dimensional array of byte. Each byte is used to represent NoData mask values for 8 correspondent pixels. If the image (or SafeArray) has an dimension of nxn, the length of the array returned from NoDataMask will be (n* n+7)/7
